Content: Michael Carrick on the touchline during Manchester United’s 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday.Photograph: Gary Oakley/EPAView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick on the touchline during Manchester United’s 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday.Photograph: Gary Oakley/EPAManchester UnitedMichael Carrick attends Manchester United training ground as club discuss his fateHead coach arrives to watch under-21s playBruno Fernandes likes Instagram post about loyaltyJamie JacksonMon 26 Oct 2026 12.57 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 16.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick was at Manchester United’s training ground on Monday afternoon as elsewhere at the ­Carrington base Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and Omar ­Berrada, the chief executive officer, deliberated over whether to sack the head coach.Carrick arrived at 1.50pm to watch the under-21s play a behind‑closed-doors game.Damning data: stats that show Michael Carrick’s luck was bound to run out | Andrew BeasleyRead moreWilcox and Berrada met at Carrington early on Monday morning after United’s3-0 defeat against ­Bournemouthon Sunday at Old Trafford that leftCarrick’s job in the balance. Wilcox departed just before 5pm and Carrick left shortly after.The defeat made it eight games without a win for Carrick’s side, who have two victories all season. United are in 16th in the Premier League, just a point above the relegation zone.If the 45-year-old Carrick is removed, Eddie Howe remains­Wilcox’s preferred candidate, with contact between the parties understood to have been made. The former Newcastle ­manager is open to taking up the position, ­subject to negotiations.Howe, 48, would be less expensive to recruit than Unai Emery, another admired manager, because Aston Villa would demand around £20m in compensation for the ­Spaniard.Julian Nagelsmann, the ­former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by ­Christopher ­Vivell, United’s director of ­recruitment, who is believed to have sounded out his fellow ­German. The pair previously worked together at RB Leipzig.Wilcox’s view may hold more sway with Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who ­controls football policy at United. Antonio Conte, who left Napoli in the summer, is another who may be in the frame.Carrick dropped Bruno Fernandes for the Bournemouth defeat for what he claimed were “pure football reasons”. This came after the 32‑year‑oldcriticised Carrick for his tacticsin the 4-1 capitulation at Como in the ­Champions League last Wednesday. The United captain was an unused substi­tute and was booed, along with other players, by fans in the ­Stretford End at the end of the defeat against Marco Rose’s side.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionOn Monday Fernandes liked an ­Instagram post that said: “Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care.” The post also said: “The person holding everything together is usually the one nobody thinks to check on.”Ineos, which is owned by ­Ratcliffe, has reportedly put FC ­Lausanne‑Sport up for sale. Ineos declined to comment when contacted by the ­Guardian. ­Lausanne-Sport are bottom of the top division in Switzerland.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarricknewsShareReuse this content

title: England Under-15s walk off pitch against Ireland in World Cup after racism allegation | Soccer | The Guardian
description: England’s match against the Republic of Ireland in new Under-15 World Cup has been abandoned after England alleged racism aimed at one of their players
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: England’s match against the Republic of Ireland in new Under-15 World Cup has been abandoned after England alleged racism aimed at one of their players
Content: England gather at the side of the pitch during their match against the Republic of Ireland, in the Under-15 World Cup, after one of their players alleged he was racially abused.Photograph: DaznView image in fullscreenEngland gather at the side of the pitch during their match against the Republic of Ireland, in the Under-15 World Cup, after one of their players alleged he was racially abused.Photograph: DaznSoccerEngland Under-15s walk off pitch against Ireland in World Cup after racism allegationMatch in new Fifa competition abandonedEngland players refuse to resume matchEd AaronsMon 26 Oct 2026 15.20 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 16.59 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEngland abandoned their Under-15 World Cup match against the Republic of Ireland on Monday after a player reported being subjected to a racist slur. Fifa confirmed it was investigating what happened in the final minute of the Group C fixture in Baku, Azerbaijan, when Ireland were leading 4-1.Footage showed an England player approaching the bench after an altercation. He is believed to have alleged an opponent called him a “monkey” and raised a complaint with the coaching staff, prompting England’s head coach, Matt Thorpe, to approach the referee.Thorpe was seen asking the referee to come over before instructing his players to leave the field. One of England’s assistant coaches subsequently told the referee: “We are reporting racism”, adding that the team did not want to continue playing.When another official approached to discuss the next steps, the assistant coach reiterated that England’s players did not want to resume the match. He also said a player was upset by the incident. Footage later showed heated exchanges between members of the coaching teams, with representatives from each side saying they were seeking to protect their players.“Fifa is aware of an incident at the Under-15 World Cup and Festival match between England and the Republic of Ireland,” said a spokesperson for world football’s governing body. “The match was abandoned by the referee following England’s refusal to continue.”The spokesperson said the official reports were being collected and that the matter would be referred to Fifa’s independent disciplinary committee, which would decide on any further action.The Football Association has not commented, but is understood to be waiting for more information. It is said to be taking the matter seriously and providing support to players and staff. The Football Association of Ireland has been contacted for comment.The inaugural Under-15 World Cup involves 189 countries and territories. Games are played in an eight-a-side format on smaller pitches, with two 20-minute halves.England, who had won their three previous matches against Cambodia, Montenegro and Nicaragua, faced Zimbabwe later on Monday, while Ireland were due to play Cambodia. Only the group winners will progress to the top-tier competition this week, with the rest of the teams divided into separate tiers depending on where they finished.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBefore the tournament, Fifa described it as “unrivalled in scale or ambition”. More than 3,000 players are taking part in 950 matches, with each team playing a minimum of nine games. Arsène Wenger, Fifa’s chief of global football development, described it as giving “players from across the world the chance to compete, to learn and to grow”.Explore more on these topicsFootballEnglandFifanewsShareReuse this content

title: Doubles players sign open letter pleading with tennis chiefs to ‘protect’ format | Tennis | The Guardian
description: More than 150 doubles players on the men’s ATP tour have signed an open letter addressed to the ATP board, imploring the men’s tennis governing bodies to reconsider controversial doubles reforms
Author: Tumaini Carayol
Headline: More than 150 doubles players on the men’s ATP tour have signed an open letter addressed to the ATP board, imploring the men’s tennis governing bodies to reconsider controversial doubles reforms
Content: Francisco Cabral, of Portugal, and JJ Tracy, of the US, react in the men’s doubles final match against Lucas Miedler and Neil Oberleitner, of AustriaPhotograph: Shi Tang/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenFrancisco Cabral, of Portugal, and JJ Tracy, of the US, react in the men’s doubles final match against Lucas Miedler and Neil Oberleitner, of AustriaPhotograph: Shi Tang/Getty ImagesTennisDoubles players sign open letter pleading with tennis chiefs to ‘protect’ formatPlans to slash games by half and prize money criticised‘Hard for players to build and sustain a doubles career’Tumaini CarayolMon 26 Oct 2026 11.55 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 16.24 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMore than 150 doubles players on the men’s ATP tour have signed an open letter addressed to the ATP board and management imploring the men’s tennis governing bodies to reconsider controversial doubles reforms and “protect” the format in professional tennis.The subject of potential reforms to the ATP has been a significant issue since players were informed in a meeting during Wimbledon that the ATP was conducting a review of its doubles regulations and potential changes could see doubles draws being halved at the ATP events in 2028. Under these proposals, ATP Masters 1000 events would host only 16 doubles teams and the main draws at ATP 500 and 250 events would accommodate only eight teams.Women’s tennis tour announces prize money parity with men in ‘major milestone’Read moreThe proposals could also lead to the total prize money distributed to doubles players being halved from 20% to 10%, with the remaining money allocated towards singles players. The news provoked significant criticism from a large group of doubles players at Wimbledon, and they have spent subsequent months organising to resist the reforms. In addition to more than 150 active players, the letter has been signed by more than 20 national federations and legends of the sport.In the open letter, the players state: “The current plans would shift about $20m (£15m) in prize money from doubles to singles, while cutting a significant number of professional opportunities for doubles specialists. That shift would make it much harder for talented players to build and sustain a doubles career. A healthy professional sport cannot rely solely on a small group of top stars; it needs pathways for players to develop, compete and earn a living.”View image in fullscreenNetherlands’ Sem Verbeek and Czechia’s Katerina Siniakova during their mixed doubles final at Wimbledon in 2025.Photograph: Kirill Kudryavtsev/AFP/Getty ImagesSem Verbeek, the 2025 Wimbledon mixed doubles champion and one of the players spearheading the campaign, told the Guardian that the doubles players feel the ATP’s potential reforms threaten the future of doubles and that the ATP has not sought to collaborate with doubles players to shape the future of the discipline.“The A to B with these proposals is really threatening not only the history, but also the present and future of the whole discipline of professional men’s doubles,” he said.“The livelihoods of a lot of players are at stake here, and not only that, I think also the dreams of any young player that wants to pursue a doubles career are really in big jeopardy.“I think that one of the big reasons that we have so much support for this open letter is to really provide the ATP with a platform to get in touch with us and make this more of a collaboration rather than a one-sided review that they keep saying is ongoing. But any real data and real numbers and real requests that we have have not been answered so far. And I think that’s why a lot of active players are so frustrated with this because we have a lot of ideas.”The ATP management views doubles as an unsustainable loss leader, and it intends to redistribute some of the money currently reserved for doubles to singles players, an initiative doubles players believe pits singles and doubles players against each other despite the fact that they are all members of the same association.“The main message that we want to send is the ATP really has to ­balance short-term economic growth with the legacy that it has built,” Verbeek said. “We understand that the ATP and ­tennis as a whole is entertainment, is a business but you also have a responsibility to all of your fans worldwide to protect and grow the legacy of both disciplines of your sport.“It’s been clear so far I think for a lot of people, if you look at how inaccessible doubles is from a viewership standpoint, that the ATP has under-invested and under-marketed the discipline so far. So we really just want to invite the ATP to really meaning­ful collaborations and meaningful discussions on how we can grow this part of the sport without damaging the future of it and allowing people to have a celebratory career in doubles. And I think that’s part of the reason that so many legends have signed on.“For some reason the generation of decision makers that are in the ATP right now feel like a doubles career is not a real tennis career. And that to us is ludicrous. It should be celebrated. It’s a discipline that has provided a lot of history and should provide a lot of future and it shouldn’t be looked at as, let’s say, a failed singles career or something like that.”This month the ATP announced widespread reforms to the calendar, schedule and rule book. In a Q&A attributed to the ATP chief executive, Andrea Gaudenzi, on the ATP website, the men’s tennis governing body addressed its potential doubles reforms. “Doubles will continue to be a core part of the ATP Tour,” ­Gaudenzi wrote. “The review is focused on identifying a model that gives the discipline a sustainable long-term future, works effectively for tournaments and fans and supports the wider player pathway.”Explore more on these topicsTennisnewsShareReuse this content

title: Liam Dawson reveals England are ‘gutted’ after ODI series setback against Pakistan | England cricket team | The Guardian
description: Liam Dawson has revealed that the England cricket squad are ‘gutted’ after two agonising defeats have left their chances of making the ODI tri-series final hanging by a thread
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Liam Dawson has revealed that the England cricket squad are ‘gutted’ after two agonising defeats have left their chances of making the ODI tri-series final hanging by a thread
Content: Liam Dawson has become an integral part of England white-ball squad.Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/ReutersView image in fullscreenLiam Dawson has become an integral part of England white-ball squad.Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/ReutersEngland cricket teamLiam Dawson reveals England are ‘gutted’ after ODI series setback against Pakistan‘We were desperate to win’Spinner believes defeats are useful learning experiencesGuardian sportand agenciesMon 26 Oct 2026 09.15 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 17.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLiam Dawson has revealed England’s disappointment after the two ­agonising defeatsto Sri Lankaand Pakistanthat have left making the ODI tri-series final in serious doubt. “That ­changing room is gutted, we’re desperate to win,” he said.TNT Sports close to securing live UK rights for England white-ball cricket tour of AustraliaRead moreTo reach the final, England need Pakistan to beat Sri Lanka on Tuesday and then they have to thrash Gary Kirsten’s men on Thursday, but Dawson is optimistic the losses can help them in the World Cup in 12 months’ time in southern Africa.“If you look at the last two games, we’ve been in positions where we should have won, so that is a ­massive positive as a group,” he said. “To lose those two games from a position we’re in is frustrating because we should have won those games.“If, in a year’s time, we do get to those situations again and bank on our previous experiences then we’ll look back at this tri-series as a huge positive.”The 36-year-old said he is not drawing any conclusions from ­usurping Adil Rashid. For more than a decade, the leg-spinner has been the No 1 spinner for England in white-ball formats and he needs 26 more dismissals to become their all-time leading one-day wicket-taker.After missing September’s home series win over Sri Lanka because of an injury, Rashid has been overlooked for the defeats to Sri Lanka and ­Pakistan.The explanation given is Dawson’s skiddy slow left-armers are more suited to the conditions in ­Rawalpindi and Lahore, with Rashid expensive in his only tournament outingagainst Pakistan last week.In Rashid’s absence, ­Dawson has impressed, but a ­bowling unit light on experience has been exposed as England let seemingly surefire wins slip away.The former England captain Nasser Hussain told Sky Sports last week that Rashid’s recent performances had “dropped off”, although Dawson believes the double World Cup winner remains a stellar operator.“I don’t think I can be compared to Adil, he’s a phenomenal bowler,” he said. “You don’t play 165 ODIs and become a bad bowler. I don’t think you can compare us at all because we’re so different in our roles in the team. He’s a fantastic bowler, he’s been exceptional for England and I think he still will be.”Without an express paceman or mystery spinner, England let ­Pakistan off the hook from 154 for nine chasing 242 in Lahore on Sunday as Shadab Khan and the No 11, Haris Rauf, sealed an extraordinary win for the hosts.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe pair’s 89-run stand set a record for the highest 10th-wicket partnership in a successful chase and came three days after England, despite Harry Brook smashing a double hundred, were unable to defend 429 against Sri LankaAfter being a fringe England player for much of his career, Dawson has established himself as a mainstay in the T20 side under Brook and is more involved in the ODI setup.“Up until a year or so ago, I said to numerous people I didn’t think I’d play for England again,” he said. “I’ve really enjoyed the time I’ve had so far.“ You’re desperate to do well, but each time I get to play for ­England is a really special thing. I didn’t think it would happen at the age I got to so to play the amount I have in the last year and contribute has been really ­pleasing and hopefully that can continue.”Dawson retired from first-class cricket in May after 19 years with Hampshire and having played four Test matches, but he will not be reversing that decision even if approached by the new England Test head coach, Stephen ­Fleming. “Those days are gone,” he said.Explore more on these topicsEngland cricket teamSri Lanka cricket teamPakistan cricket teamCricketnewsShareReuse this content

title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement  | La Liga | The Guardian
description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at the Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at the Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points
Content: Real Madrid’s players converge after Kylian Mbappé’s late winner at Camp Nou.Photograph: Albert Gea/ReutersView image in fullscreenReal Madrid’s players converge after Kylian Mbappé’s late winner at Camp Nou.Photograph: Albert Gea/ReutersLa LigaMourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statementIt was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three pointsSid LoweMon 26 Oct 2026 12.35 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 17.13 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJosé Mourinho had already done thepor qué?,the printoutand the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in theclásicoon Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists.He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out.Davide Ancelotti wants to make a name for himself – will he do it at Lille?Read more“We have the best goalkeeper in the world, but none of us cried because Thibaut couldn’t play,” Mourinho said. Plenty might have felt like it, more reason to be fearful. But the coach called Andriy Lunin, the substitute goalkeeper so serious that he bought a roll of artificial turf and spent the pandemic diving round the living room of his flat, and told him this was his moment: “You train to play, not to sit on the bench, so go on.” As for the rest of them, the manager told them nothing changes: the plan remains in place. By the time they headed back to the dressing room, “Fucking get in!” echoing along the Camp Nou corridor, so it had proved.Thirteen years later, Mourinho was back in Barcelona for aclásicoand he had guided Madrid to a 2-1 win. It wasn’t supposed to be like this, or maybe it was. Barcelona, the team who had won nine in a row,banging in 4.3 goals per game, had been beaten by Madrid, the team who had lost twice already and, truth be told, were mostly just not very good. The night it could have been all over, the title race done when it’s not even in November, was instead the night it finally started. “If you leave here nine points behind, it’s very heavy psychologically; if it’s six, it’s more balanced; if it’s three, that’s different,” Mourinho said.View image in fullscreenJosé Mourinho returned to where it all began to continue his unbeaten streak against Barcelona.Photograph: Joan Monfort/APThis was different, and so is the season now. Counting theclásicosall those years ago, Mourinho racked up his sixth consecutive meeting withBarcelonawithout defeat, and there had been no parked bus, nor many lumps kicked. They didn’t just desperately hang on, although there was a moment when Dean Huijsen saved a shot with his face. Nor had they just waited for a moment, resisting and then robbing it, even if João Cancelo did insist: “That’s Madrid; they don’t have many chances but they score them.” The final shot count said 18-10 to Barcelona, and possession was 62% Barcelona’s.“The way we won is important: you can win luckily or by defending a lot. But we won with calmness and totally deservedly. We did it by being organised, concentrated and having the courage to come out from the back,” Mourinho said. And if that might have been pushing it a little – and, let’s face it, the analyses might be different had Lunin not made an astonishing save from Gerard Martín or Lamine Yamal’s second-half shot not faded just past the post – he had a point.Barcelona were not at their best. They had been hurried and imprecise, Rodri telling his teammates to lower their “pulse rate” as they came out for the second half. Lamine Yamal somehow missed an extraordinary chance just before the break. And when they did tighten the screw in the second half, they couldn’t break the wall. Xavi Espart was forced off, yet another injury at the back, the failure to sign a centre-back in the spotlight again. Yet this was still a faster, more aggressive, tighter Madrid than anyone expected. Asked to define it, Lunin went for “discipline and attitude”. And if that is partly about occasion, the least you can ask for, it’s more than you sometimes get.View image in fullscreenAndriy Lunin stepped up for Real Madrid in the absence of the ill Thibaut Courtois.Photograph: Jose Breton/APBesides, it was also more than that. More than Marc Cucurella getting under Lamine Yamal’s skin, although he certainly succeeded. They went for the space beyond Barcelona’s full-backs: superb in his firstclásico, aged 19, Yan Diomandé –the left winger– got more touches than any Madrid player, and protected his full-back as well. But it was more than that, too. More than the wonderful winning goal, a flash of inspiration with Jude Bellingham going all Nureyev, the ball flitting between his feet and Gabriel Jesus’s legs, pirouetting to release Eduardo Camavinga. This was a team with an idea and a victory that vindicated their manager, some kind of resurrection.Before the game, Rodri said that one of Madrid’s tricks is to convince you that they’re not that good, but insisted he wouldn’t fall into that trap. Still he felt that plan particularly. Pedri did too. Bellingham dealt with Rodri, Bernardo Silva with Pedri. Pressed and tired too, according to Hansi Flick, neither truly took control. The inclusion of Arda Güler and Silva – the surprise in the middle, starting his first league game in six weeks – underlined an intention for Madrid to keep the ball when they could. They actually had a midfield, which was new. From the back they tried to build, draw Barcelona in. And if a time came when they had to wait, to put bodies in before the ball, well, they would do that too. Six times Barcelona shots were blocked. At least twice more, shots were taken from their toes. At the other end, meanwhile, Madrid attacked with an intent and an incision that probably drew the clearer chances: the xG showed 1.19 v 1.94.Quick GuideLa Liga resultsShowAlaves 1-1 Malaga, Rayo Vallecano 0-3 Elche, Racing Santander 2-1 Espanyol, Valencia 1-2 Villarreal, Atlético 1-0 Deportiva A Coruna, A Bilbao 4-0 Getafe, Celta Vigo 0-0 Real Betis, Real Sociedad 2-1 Levante, Barcelona 1-2 Real MadridMonday:Sevilla v OsasunaWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Victory puts Madrid three points behind Barcelona and, Federico Valverde claimed, “will give us a kickstart”. It has taken 10 weeks but it’s game on.Hay liga, as they like to say. There is league. There is Madrid, too. Something has shifted,starting in Rome, where 70 dreadful minutes gave way to 20 pretty good ones, another inexplicable comeback actually having something of an explanation, too. The changes were impossible to ignore. Valverde and Aurélien Tchouaméni no longer the partnership in the middle, Valverde going to right-back instead. Güler playing. Diomandé playing. And, yes, Vinícius Júniornotplaying. “I’m not stubborn; I can change,” Mourinho said. Madrid have won five in succession now; something was seen that night, a way ahead. They’ve won every game since Vinícius was suspended, facile and perhaps even cruel though that may be to say. And since Mourinho grew a beard, if you believe in that kind of thing.View image in fullscreenKylian Mbappé celebrates the goal that leaves Real Madrid only three points behind Barcelona in the league.Photograph: Albert Gea/ReutersBefore theclásico, Mourinho had said it wasn’t fair to compare his team, a side in construction and a long way from the finished product, to Barcelona. He insisted that he was still getting to know his players; he hadn’t been there long, after all. After theclásico, he admitted: “We have improved, we can’t hide that.” The idea has shifted, almost like it was an epiphany: “I’ve learned something about the middle of the pitch; I have learned that a mixture is better, that it is better to have a combination of qualities than two players of similar characteristics.” In short, Tchouaméni and Valverde doesn’t work. There needs to be some football in there somewhere, and so a shift started. Sunday came as a kind of confirmation, a hope, an identity emerging.“The best Madrid is born at the Camp Nou,” ran the headline in El País. “Madrid are here now,” AS’s cover said. “I won’t let them have their heads on the moon; if we win this and then don’t win at the Sardinero, it won’t mean much,” Mourinho said, but this was a start, not just an end in itself. At full time, Mourinho headed on to the pitch and shook Lunin’s hand as all around players embraced. High in the north-east corner, Madrid’s fans stayed and sang. Back home, Courtois was watching. He had “a horrible night” on Saturday, they said, but now he was feeling a little better. They all were.PosTeamPGDPts1Barcelona1029272Atletico Madrid1012253Real Madrid1015244Real Betis102205Real Sociedad101196Sevilla9-2147Alaves103128Athletic Bilbao93129Celta Vigo1031210Villarreal1011211Deportivo A Coruna1001112Osasuna9-81113Racing Santander10-111114Levante10-31015Elche10-31016Rayo Vallecano9-8917Getafe10-10918Espanyol10-2819Valencia10-10620Malaga10-125Explore more on these topicsLa LigaReal MadridBarcelonaJosé MourinhoEuropean club footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: England fret over Fin Smith’s fitness for looming Australia match | England rugby union team | The Guardian
description: Steve Borthwick has been handed a dilemma at 10, with the Northampton fly-half unable to join the England training camp this week
Author: Robert Kitson
Headline: Steve Borthwick has been handed a dilemma at 10, with the Northampton fly-half unable to join the England training camp this week
Content: Fin Smith came off injured during the weekend Prem game between Northampton and Leicester.Photograph: Luke Hastings/Wired Photos/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenFin Smith came off injured during the weekend Prem game between Northampton and Leicester.Photograph: Luke Hastings/Wired Photos/ShutterstockEngland rugby union teamEngland fret over Fin Smith’s fitness for looming Australia matchBorthwick responds by calling up Charlie AtkinsonGuy Pepper and Benhard van Rensburg also doubtsRobert KitsonMon 26 Oct 2026 14.30 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 16.17 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEngland are fretting over the fitness of the fly-half Fin Smith in the lead-up to the Nations Championship home opener against Australia on 8 November. The Northampton player ­damaged a calf in the second halfagainst Leicester on Saturdayand will be unable to join the national squad who have a three-day training camp in Bagshot this week.Marcus Smith produces timely reminder of his class as Harlequins sink SaracensRead moreLosing Smith so close to the ­Wallabies game would be a significant blow given the 24-year-old started at 10 in all three of England’s Tests in July and was instrumental in Saints’ domestic title triumph last season.England’s management say they remain hopeful he will be back in time to face Australia but, with limited preparation time available, there will inevitably be some disruption to Steve ­Borthwick’s plans.Borthwick has responded by ­calling up ­Gloucester’s Charlie ­Atkinson as cover, with Marcus Smith and George Ford the other ­specialist 10s in the squad. Since deposing Ford afterEngland’s defeat against Ireland in the Six Nations, Fin Smith has staked a firm claim and is very much the man in possession of the 10 jersey. Marcus Smith’s last start at fly-half for England was against Ireland in ­Dublin in the opening round of the 2025 Six Nations.There will be an official update on Smith’s condition on Tuesday with injury doubts hanging over several other players. Bath’s Guy Pepper appeared to be in pain as he limped off against Gloucester on Friday, while Benhard Janse van ­Rensburg has not featured since sufferingsustaining a heavy concussion in Bristol’s second Prem game of the season.The inside centre Seb Atkinson is also unable to train this week but has not ruled out playing for Gloucester at Northampton on Saturday. It leaves Borthwick and the squad’s other specialist centres – Henry Slade, Joe Marchant, Max Ojomoh and Fraser Dingwall – waiting to see what will unfold before the formal squad announcement next Monday.Marchant, for one, is delighted to be back in the frame for the first time since the 2023 World Cup. He then moved to Paris to play for Stade Français, ­having previously been told his England career was over, but is now back and eligible again after joining Sale Sharks.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe 30-year-old Marchant, who married Alan Shearer’s daughter Hollie this year, said he would love to feature at the World Cup in Australia next year. “When I was a kid I wanted to play for England and that’s not changed,” he said.Explore more on these topicsEngland rugby union teamNations ChampionshipRugby unionnewsShareReuse this content

title: Bookies fear budget hit but gaming machine self-harm killed off the old-fashioned shops | Horse racing | The Guardian
description: A wholesale plunder of local communities via casino-gaming took place and racing was content to sit on sidelines
Author: Greg Wood
Headline: A wholesale plunder of local communities via casino-gaming took place and racing was content to sit on sidelines
Content: A punter tries out a gambling machine during the opening of a new William Hill betting shop.Photograph: Daniel Hambury/PAView image in fullscreenA punter tries out a gambling machine during the opening of a new William Hill betting shop.Photograph: Daniel Hambury/PATalking HorsesHorse racingAnalysisBookies fear budget hit but gaming machine self-harm killed off the old-fashioned shopsGreg WoodA wholesale plunder of local communities via casino-gaming took place and racing was content to sit on sidelinesMon 26 Oct 2026 14.35 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 18.48 EDTShareHas it really been almost a year since racing’s last bout of Budget-related anxiety? Apparently so, because havingsuccessfully persuaded Rachel Reeves to exempt racingfrom a (modest) hike in betting duty in 2025, here we are again, nervously anticipating Wednesday’s budget amid warnings that John Healey could effectively sound the death-knell for high-street betting shops.Healey is widely expected to raise the rate of machine games duty (MGD) in the budget, a move which could, according to some predictions, lead to the closure of thousands of high-street shops with significant knock-on effects for racing’s income from off-course gambling.The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan WilsonRead moreThe prospect of a significant hike in MGD this week was initially floated bya report from the Social Market Foundation(SMF) thinktank in June. The report recommended doubling the duty rate on the profits from high-street gaming machines, from 20% to 40%, to reflect the significantly higher rates of harm associated with machine gaming compared to traditional betting on racing and sport.The gambling industry’s response was swift and indignant. Citinga report from the consultancy firm Regulus Partners,the industry warned that if Healey took the SMF’s advice, up to 4,000 of the UK’s 5,500 betting shops could be forced to close over the next three years. That, in turn, could cost the racing industry an estimated £92m in annual income – a third of its total from betting.The British Horseracing Authority also expressed its concern. “This would have devastating consequences for British racing,” Greg Swift, the BHA’s director of communications and corporate affairs, said in a statement this month, “hitting prize money, Levy funding and our ability to continue investing in our world-leading equine welfare and veterinary research projects.”Subsequent rumours ahead of Wednesday’s budget suggest that Healey is considering a less dramatic rise in MGD, from 20% to 25%. Yet even this, according to the gambling industry, could lead to hundreds of shop closures and tens of millions in lost revenue for racing.So, is the end really nigh for the high-street betting shop? Its demise has, after all, been forecast with some regularity over the last couple of decades since the advent of online gambling, and above all when the campaign to cut the maximum stake on the high-street fixed odds betting terminals (FOBTs), from £100 to £2, was at its height.View image in fullscreenA man checks the form before he places a wager in a betting shop.Photograph: Scott Barbour/Getty ImagesSuggestions at the time that most or all of the UK’s shops would be shuttered within months if the cut were imposed proved to be a long way short of the mark. The current total of around 5,500 shops is well below the 9k around a decade ago, but that also reflects the fact that the gambling market as a whole, and among younger generations in particular, is increasingly moving online.At the same time, though, there can be little doubt, however, that racing remains painfully exposed to a major reduction in the number of shops. The sport’s income from the retail sector is tied to media rights contracts for live pictures and data agreed on a “per-shop” basis. The Regulus report suggests that racing receives around £27k in media rights and Levy payments from the average shop’s total annual revenue of £440k.If a sport that derives a significant chunk of its income via betting is caught up in the fallout from a tax rise on casino-gaming, however, there is an extent to which it can only have itself to blame.The BHA took offence when, shortly after being installed as prime minister,Andy Burnham lumped in betting shopsalongside vape shops and adult gaming arcades as undesirable presences on the high street. But if an outlet cannot absorb a 5% rise in MGD, there is an argument that it is no longer a betting shop at all. It is a mini-casino, with betting on the side.At the turn of the century, a betting shop (or maybe two) was a familiar and largely accepted part of the high street landscape. But that consensus was swept away in the headlong rush to squeeze as many shops as possible into areas of high population density, in order to install the maximum number of four FOBTs in each one.It was the bookies themselves that killed off the old-fashioned betting shop, amid a cynical and deliberate orgy of corporate greed that sucked hundreds of millions of pounds from what were already the UK’s most deprived areas. They did not want or need five or six “betting” shops in a row, but they got them anyway. At one stage in the mid-2010s, there were 18 on the main high street in Hackney alone.Quick GuideGreg Wood's Tuesday tipsShowCatterick Bridge12.40 Cyberspace 1.10 Bladey Lady 1.40 Barmyblade 2.10 Knicks 2.40 Marching Mac 3.10 Havana Rum 3.40 Corsican Caper 4.10 Pol RogerNewcastle12.56 Wilde’s Legacy 1.26 Royal Time 2.01 Cawthorne Cracker 2.31 Silver Hill 3.01 North Of Richmond 3.31 Rule Me In (nb) 4.01 Mon MisselBangor-On-Dee1.46 Glance Of Glory 2.16 Rattlin Home 2.46 Hornica 3.16 Just Golden 3.46 Inedit D’Amour 4.16 The Big BreacWolverhampton4.30 Sant Alessio 5.00 Show Me Glory 5.30 What A Go I’ve Had 6.00 On Key 6.30 Distillate 7.00 Bessie Wallis 7.30 Pulsar Star 8.00 Kaaranah (nap) 8.30 Gustav GravesWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.It was a wholesale plunder of local communities via casino-gaming, and even as the campaign to restrict FOBT stakes gained irresistible momentum, racing was largely content to sit on the sidelines and keep counting the cash from its media rights deal. While Matt Hancock, the culture secretary in 2018, was consulting on whether to cut the maximum FOBT stake to £2, the BHAactively supported the gambling industry’swarnings of imminent disaster – including wholesale shop closures – if the cut was imposed.So while the rise of online gambling was always going to see a steady decline in the number of betting shops, it is thanks to the FOBTs that there will be very few in the general public to mourn their passing, if or when they close their doors. And racing, which did little or nothing to stand up for betting while the FOBT scandal unfolded, can have few genuine grounds for complaint if, after Wednesday’s budget, it continues to pay the price for its complicity.Explore more on these topicsHorse racingTalking HorsesGamblingSport bettinganalysisShareReuse this content

title: WSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progress | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start
Author: Sophie Downey
Headline: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start
Content: (Left to right): Eva Olid, Birmingham’s Wilma Leidhammar and Alessia Russo of Arsenal.Composite: Getty Images, ReutersView image in fullscreen(Left to right): Eva Olid, Birmingham’s Wilma Leidhammar and Alessia Russo of Arsenal.Composite: Getty Images, ReutersWomen's Super LeagueWSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progressGunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning startSuzanne Wrack,Tom Garry,Sophie Downey,Emillia Hawkinsand Mitul SamjiMon 26 Oct 2026 07.59 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 14.37 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWill derby win kick-start Arsenal’s season?The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result.Suzanne WrackMatch report: Tottenham 1-2 ArsenalGodfrey a star in the makingView image in fullscreenFreya Godfrey of London City LionessesPhotograph: Clare Overfield/SPP/ShutterstockIs Freya Godfrey England’s future? That’s what Alexia Putellas thinks of her London City Lionesses teammate, and the Spain icon heaped praise on the 21-year-old winger after she scored in her second consecutive WSL game. Godfrey – who made her senior England debut earlier this month against Greece – capitalised on a Khiara Keating mistake to score in the 2-2 draw with Liverpool on Sunday and her all-round display delighted Putellas, who told Sky Sports: “She can arrive where she really wants. I always tell her, she’s a star girl. She will be the future of this club. She has to keep working like she is doing now. She will be the future of England as well as the present.”TGUnited show progress under OlidManchester United’s display in Sunday’s derby draw was night and day compared to their most recent previous home league fixture against a title challenger, when they were torn apart ina 5-0 defeat at home against Chelseajust six weeks ago. Against Manchester City on Sunday they competed toe-to-toe with the defending champions, and while it would be wrong to suggest that Eva Olid’s team are anywhere near the finished article, their improvements are striking, both with and without the ball. Olid feels that heavy defeat early in her tenure actually helped her side. “It was a hard week after Chelsea but sometimes you need a difficult moment to happen, to react and see exactly where the problems [were] or the things we had to solve as a team,” she said. “It had to happen to now be the team we are.”Tom GarryMatch report: Manchester United 1-1 Manchester CityBirmingham earn first win of WSL returnBirmingham’s first win of the WSL season came in the first encounter between league newcomers this season. Followingan impressive point at the Emiratesthe week before,the 1-0 win over Charlton marked another key step as Amy Merricks’ side continue to settle into the top flight. The Blues were almost made to pay for their profligacy in front of goal against a familiar foe from last season in WSL2. They dominated proceedings and created 20 chances in total but registered just five on target. Océane Hurtré and Lisa Naalsund rattled the crossbar while Lily Crosthwaite missed three gilt-edged opportunities before Wilma Leidhammar struck a 68th minute-winner. “That was the most important thing today,” Merricks said. “We needed to pick up three points and we delivered that. I don’t think the performance was our finest. You could feel the caginess across the pitch and that is something we need to work on. We are in a better place, and we keep pushing.”Sophie Downeyskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDepth the difference as Chelsea produce comebackView image in fullscreenMelvine Malard displayed her class as Chelsea despatched Crystal Palace.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/ReutersFor 51 minutes on Sunday afternoon, it felt like it might just be one of those days for Chelsea. Despite dominating the first half – they created 12 opportunities to Crystal Palace’s four and registered 20 touches in the opposition box – they found themselves trailing and running out of ideas. A key difference between the two sides, however, is the strength in depth available to their respective managers. In bringing on Erin Cuthbert and Sandy Baltimore at half-time, Sonia Bompastor was able to call on the services of two experienced internationals. Cuthbert added a crucial bite to the midfield that had been lacking in the first half while Baltimore set up Melvine Malard to put the Blues in front before scoring from the spot to confirm the three points. In contrast, Jo Potter made just three substitutions with the first coming in the 77th minute. It is this ability to change things from the bench that truly illustrates the gap in class between the eight-time WSL champions and the league newcomers.SDSørensen makes statement against former clubBrian Sørensen and his Aston Villa side came away with a 3-2 win against Everton. Sørensen, who took over from Natalia Arroyo last month, faced the Merseyside club for the first time since hisGoodison Park exit in February. Villa dominated the clash and went 3-0 up within 50 minutes thanks to goals from Noelle Maritz and Amalie Vangsgaard, but they were given a scare following a late comeback push with Holly McNamara and Noémie Mouchon both scoring. Villa saw the game out to take three points – just. Nevertheless, Sørensen will be thrilled with the outcome, especially as it moved his team up to eighth. It also marked the first time since the 2024-25 campaign that Villa have won back-to-back games. “I’m happy, it was overall a good performance,” the interim head coach said. “Of course, maybe they got a bit too excited at the end but I also think we had the opportunities to kill the game off a lot sooner. But three points is three points, that’s all that matters.”Emillia HawkinsSymonds’ stunner inspires Brighton winMaisie Symonds’ stunning strike set Brighton on course for a 3-0 victory over West Ham. The Brighton captain broke the deadlock in the 29th minute, meeting a headed clearance with a first-time strike from distance that swerved beyond West Ham goalkeeper Constance Picaud-Inconnu and kissed the post on its way in. It was her second goal of the season, rewarding Brighton’s early dominance. Fran Kirby doubled the lead in the 63rd minute before Kiko Seike struck three minutes later. Brighton’s head coach, Arturo Ruiz, called it his side’s “most complete” performance of the season, praising their confidence and tactical adaptability. Symonds said Brighton “got control” in the second half. It was the Seagulls’ first Women’s Super League clean sheet of the campaign.Mitul SamjiExplore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueWomen's footballArsenal WomenTottenham Hotspur WomenManchester United WomenManchester City WomenBirmingham City WomenfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Wolff hails Antonelli’s US Grand Prix demolition as the Italian’s ‘best race yet’  | Formula One 2026 | The Guardian
description: The Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has paid tribute to his driver Kimi Antonelli and hailed his victory at the US Grand Prix as the Italian’s ‘best race yet’
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: The Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has paid tribute to his driver Kimi Antonelli and hailed his victory at the US Grand Prix as the Italian’s ‘best race yet’
Content: Kimi Antonelli and his Mercedes team show their delight after his US Grand Prix victory put him within sight of the F1 title.Photograph: Eric Gay/APView image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli and his Mercedes team show their delight after his US Grand Prix victory put him within sight of the F1 title.Photograph: Eric Gay/APFormula One 2026Wolff hails Antonelli’s US Grand Prix demolition as the Italian’s ‘best race yet’Driver on verge of claiming championship in Mexico‘The drive was exceptional. He outperformed the car’Giles Richardsin AustinMon 26 Oct 2026 05.32 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 15.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Mercedes team principal, Toto Wolff, has paid tribute to Kimi Antonelli, who all but closed out his first Formula One world cham­pionship with avictory at the US Grand Prixthat Wolff described as the Italian’s best race.Wolff was at pains to point out the considerable efforts made by a number of other people in bringing the young Italian to the verge of a record-breaking title.After his victory at the Circuit of the Americas, Antonelli needs to ­finish ninth or better at the Mexican Grand Prix this weekend. He could even finish outside the points as long as neither his teammate, George Russell, nor ­Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, the other drivers in the running, win the race. If he seals the title in Mexico City he will become F1’s youngest world champion at 20 years old.Kimi Antonelli looks forward to drivers’ title after victory in US Grand PrixRead moreAntonelli led from pole position on Sunday with a controlled, ­dominant run largely at the front of the field, for his ninth success of the season.“On Kimi’s side, the main headline is that [it is] for me the best race that he’s delivered,” Wolff said. “Getting off the start with the ­inferior tyre and then controlling it at all times. ­Exceptional. I think he’s ­outperformed the car.”When asked if it matched­Antonelli’s superb drive from 19th to victoryat the Italian Grand Prixin September, Wolff acknowledged it was special, but that Austin was up there with that drive.Antonelli concurred. “Monza was a super special one and one I will remember for ever,” he said. “But this one, probably in terms of execution, was better because the way we built the performance throughout the weekend was very good.”Wolff believed it was all the more impressive given how difficult Antonelli’s rookie season had been in 2025 when at times he struggled with the car and made mistakes that caused some to question whether Mercedes had been correct to promote him to the team so soon.View image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli celebrates winning the US Grand Prix.Photograph: Bryn Lennon/Formula 1/Getty ImagesThose are doubts he feels Antonelli has comprehensively silenced. “There are many ­people that said last year after nine races ­without points he shouldn’t be in a ­Mercedes,” Wolff said. “People in other teams that said he shouldn’t even be inFormula One.“All of that now is extremely ­satisfying to see what he’s able to deliver, how he’s working with the team, with Bono [race engineer, Peter Bonnington] and yielding the results. But it wasn’t an easy road.“It’s been 30 or more years that I’ve tried to understand racing drivers’ brains and I still don’t know what has happened over the winter. His ­ability to process and deliver something that’s outstanding, which we didn’t see coming.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMercedes took on Antonelli as part of their driver development ­programme when he was 12 years old and have supported him through karting and in the feeder series to F1.Wolff was the driving force behind bringing Antonelli into the team to take Hamilton’s seat when the Briton left for Ferrari. Wolff was insistent he felt the youngster was ready to step up and he maintained that ­Antonelli’s success should not be viewed as ­having come from nowhere, but rather the product of many years and the input of many people.“I wasn’t the one responsible for it,” Wolff said. “It was teamwork. It was our junior team around [the ­Mercedes driver development adviser] Gwen [Lagrue] that dis­covered him when he was 11.“Credit to that group that have developed him over the many years. I read an interview [with the Ferrari vice-chair] Piero Ferrari last week where he said: ‘What a talent, he reminds me of Niki Lauda.’ And I’m thinking, people don’t get that this is the work of nine years.“The development of nine years, the hardship over nine years, the integration of the team, the ­working with the engineers, millions in the ­development of his career, of his ­ability, of his character together with his parents. It’s just not that it landed like this.”Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Kimi AntonelliToto WolffFormula OneMercedes GPMotor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Serbia’s Student List preparing for talks on forming government despite no clear leader | World news | The Guardian
description: Non-hierarchical movement is seeking to ‘rebuild society’ in Balkan country after years of authoritarian rule
Author: Jon Henley
Headline: Non-hierarchical movement is seeking to ‘rebuild society’ in Balkan country after years of authoritarian rule
Content: Young Serbians celebrate outside the national assembly building in Belgrade on Monday after Student List won the country’s parliamentary elections.Photograph: Armin Durgut/APView image in fullscreenYoung Serbians celebrate outside the national assembly building in Belgrade on Monday after Student List won the country’s parliamentary elections.Photograph: Armin Durgut/APWorld newsSerbia’s Student List preparing for talks on forming government despite no clear leaderNon-hierarchical movement is seeking to ‘rebuild society’ in Balkan country after years of authoritarian ruleJon Henleyand Ana Milosavljevic in BelgradeMon 26 Oct 2026 13.12 EDTFirst published on Mon 26 Oct 2026 12.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSerbia’s triumphant but untested Student List movement is preparing to start talks on forming a government capable of reversing 14 years of increasingly authoritarian nationalist rule, aftera seismic weekend election win.Supporters of the movement, which has no experience of government, took to the streets in the west Balkan country on Monday after the strongman former president, Aleksandar Vučić, was defeated in a historic landslide.Vučić conceded defeat late on Sunday, bringing his domination of Serbian politics to an abrupt end and capping two years of anti-government protests triggered by the collapse of a canopy at the Novi Sad railway station that killed 16 people.Cheers, fireworks and flags after Vučić concedes defeat in Serbian election – in picturesRead moreWith 100% of ballot samples counted, projected results from the Centre for Free Elections and Democracy in Belgrade showed the Student List on 53% of the vote, giving it 141 MPs in the 250-seat parliament, while Vučić’s Serbian Progressive party (SNS) won 39%, giving it 103. The remaining seats went to national minority party lists.As yet, there are few clues as to how the winning movement, built around collective decision-making, will actually govern. Its candidates included academics, actors and farmers as well as students, but it is deliberately leaderless with no hierarchy, so it is unclear who it will appoint as the prime minister and cabinet.Prominent Student List figures include: ​Ilija Srdanović, a cardiologist who headed the candidate list; Dejan Šoškić, a former central bank governor; and Radomir Saičić, a chemistry professor at Belgrade ​University who spoke on behalf ‌of the List after its ​victory.Much like Péter Magyar’s Tisza party, which ended Viktor Orbán’s 16 years of illiberal government in Hungary this spring, the List faces public institutions staffed with civil servants loyal to the outgoing regime, complicating the task of institutional overhaul.“Everyone in the student movement, and every candidate on the list, has a complete and very clear understanding of the weight of the responsibility before us,” said Ana Mirković, a university educationist, psychologist and Student List candidate.0:42Drone footage shows crowds in Belgrade celebrating defeat of Aleksandar Vučić – video“We do not see the election result as gaining power and privileges, but as taking on a historic debt to our own people and to our own children.”Mirković told the Guardian the movement’s first priority was “the social and psychological detoxification” of the country.Vučić’s 14-year rule has been described as a “textbook regime” of autocracy, with his party extending control over the media, judiciary and other state institutions and elections marred by registration irregularities, media bias and voter bribes.The students’ platform centres on a pledge to fight corruption and restore the rule of law, including creating an independent police unit accountable to prosecutors, not the interior ministry, and a purge of police officers linked to organised crime.View image in fullscreenStudent List supporters in Belgrade react to the rightwing Serbian Progressive party conceding defeat on Sunday.Photograph: Marko Drobnjaković/APIt also aims to ban appointments of party loyalists to state-owned companies and to promote financial accountability and public scrutiny – by new independent bodies – of all major state infrastructure contracts ⁠to curb the misuse of public funds.Mirković said the new government would dismantle a “system of intimidation” that encouraged “fear and polarisation”, by “urgently opening up” the media, putting an end to pressure on public-sector workers and “stopping institutional violence”.She added that the aim was to “rebuild society from the ground up: full disclosure of all contracts and financial flows; depoliticising and strengthening the judiciary; renewing the education and healthcare systems”, and that state capture should “never again” be possible.The Student List deliberately kept divisive foreign policy issues, including relations with the EU and Russia, in the background. The Kremlin said on Monday it hoped the new leaders “understand that cooperation with Russia is in Serbia’s interests”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every daySign up toHeadlines EuropeA digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week dayEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDušan Vučićević, an analyst, said that, from the outset, the movement “insisted as much as possible that Serbia must first and foremost address domestic political issues – the literal dismantling of every institution, from the national to the local level”.The students’ win marks a profound political shift in Serbia and could potentially offer inspiration to other student movements that have cropped up acrossEuropein recent weeks demanding better education standards and prospects.However, Vučićević said it was distinct from other protests. “This experiment in grassroots democracy ultimately secured more than 50% of the vote,” he told Agence France-Presse, but it was “unclear whether a similar model could work in other countries”.Nikola Burazer, programme director at the Belgrade-based Centre for Contemporary Politics, said on Monday that the movement’s decision-making process also needed to “be sped up”, as its process for choosing candidates “actually took a long time – months”.‘This is a symbol for Europe’: streets of Belgrade resound with joy after Vučić defeatRead moreHe added: “After people are done celebrating and thinking about what happened yesterday, we will focus a bit more on what’s coming up, and how the government will look. Twenty-four hours ago that all seemed like a fantasy.”On Sunday, Vučić, who maintained close ties with Russia throughout his tenure, blamed his party’s defeat on “the direct support of various European countries and the US deep state, the one that is also against President Trump”.International leaders, meanwhile, joined a chorus of welcome to the students on Monday. “This is clearly a new chapter in the history of the country and its people,” said the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy.“We wish ⁠Serbia success, real development, and warm ⁠relations with the European community. ​We in Ukraine thank Serbia for respecting our people, our state, and our independence. And we always celebrate our shared achievements.”The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, said Berlin would “actively support Serbia’s European path” after the victory, saying the students “with their demand for the rule of law, fighting corruption and fundamental freedoms, have reached the people”.Serbia’s constitution requires the new parliament to convene within 30 days of the official election result, and sets a 90-day deadline after that for formation of the new government.The country must also hold new presidential elections before 27 December, since Vučić stepped down to run for prime minister.Explore more on these topicsWorld newsSerbiaEuropenewsShareReuse this content

title: iPhone Duo owners report cracks in Apple’s first foldable handset | iPhone | The Guardian
description: Company says small number of devices affected by display glitch after posts appear on Reddit and social media
Author: Dan Milmo
Headline: Company says small number of devices affected by display glitch after posts appear on Reddit and social media
Content: A broken iPhone Duo. Apple confirmed some devices had been affected by a display glitch.Photograph: Surya MangiView image in fullscreenA broken iPhone Duo. Apple confirmed some devices had been affected by a display glitch.Photograph: Surya MangiiPhoneiPhone Duo owners report cracks in Apple’s first foldable handsetCompany says small number of devices affected by display glitch after posts appear on Reddit and social mediaDan MilmoGlobal technology editorMon 26 Oct 2026 15.15 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 18.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOwners of the new foldableiPhoneare reporting cracks in the device’s screen, as Apple confirmed an issue with a “small number” of units.Reports of cracks have emerged on Reddit and social media platforms since the handset went on general sale globally on Friday. Experts said there had been too few examples to determine whether there was a more serious problem with Apple’s first foldable device, which retails from $1,999 (£1,499).Apple confirmed some devices had been affected by a display glitch.“We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement,” it said.One user in Australia reported that their Duo had cracked within six hours of taking ownership of it andposted their experience on Reddit.“I was showing it to a friend, and as I opened it, I felt something around the internal hinge, underneath the screen,” they wrote alongside an image of the phone showing an apparent display malfunction where a white strip of light ran along one half of the screen.“As I continued opening it, I heard an audible crack, and the screen broke right along the hinge.”They said their local Apple store had replaced the phone immediately. The Guardian has been unable to verify the user’s claims. Another user in Australia posted that they had heard “almost a cracking noise” on their handset, which resulted in a similar screen malfunction.View image in fullscreenIPhone Duo handsets on display at an Apple store in London.Photograph: Kin Cheung/APA report by the Bloomberg news service also highlighted similar issues among users in the US and India.Apple believes the affected units are showing defects quickly after use. It said the response from early users had been “incredibly positive”.The company said demand had been “nothing short of extraordinary” for the iPhone Duo, its most high-profile product launch under the company’s new chief executive, John Ternus, whotook over from Tim Cook in September.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe device has sold out and the next round of shipments is not expected until January, according to a report in the Economic Daily, a publication based in Taiwan, the home country of Foxconn, Apple’s main device manufacturer.Francisco Jeronimo, the vice-president of data and analytics at IDC, a tech research company, said it was too early to tell whether the screen issue was significant. “This is quite common when a new product comes to market,” he said.Citingsimilar problems at Samsung in 2019, he said: “What matters now is how the company responds … Samsung experienced problems with the original Galaxy Fold in 2019, but it also showed that a fast and transparent response can contain the damage to a category.“Apple said that any customer with problems should ask for a replacement, which is the right first step.”Ben Wood, the chief analyst at the research firm CCS, said he was taking a very cautious view of the Duo screen problem and that there was as yet no evidence of a more widespread issue with the device.Explore more on these topicsiPhoneAppleComputingMobile phonesSmartphonesTelecommunications industryConsumer affairsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Shabana Mahmood launches review into murder of student Henry Nowak | Shabana Mahmood | The Guardian
description: Move comes after claims that killer had history of using threatening behaviour and an obsession with weapons
Author: Rajeev Syal
Headline: Move comes after claims that killer had history of using threatening behaviour and an obsession with weapons
Content: Henry Nowak, 18, died in December after being fatally stabbed as he walked home from a night out in Southampton.Photograph: Family handout/PAView image in fullscreenHenry Nowak, 18, died in December after being fatally stabbed as he walked home from a night out in Southampton.Photograph: Family handout/PAShabana MahmoodShabana Mahmood launches review into murder of student Henry NowakMove comes after claims that killer had history of using threatening behaviour and an obsession with weaponsRajeev SyalHome affairs editorMon 26 Oct 2026 13.30 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 13.51 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleShabana Mahmood, the home secretary, has launched a review to examine whether opportunities were missed to prevent the murder of the student Henry Nowak.It follows claims that there were several warning signs that the perpetrator, Vickrum Digwa, had a history of threatening behaviour and an obsession with weapons.Nowak, 18, died in December after being fatally stabbed as he walked home from a night out inSouthampton. He was handcuffed by police officers while bleeding to death after Digwa falsely accused Nowak of racial abuse.In police body-worn camera footage which prompted a public outcry, Nowak was heard repeatedly saying: “I’ve been stabbed,” to which an officer replied: “Don’t think you have, mate.”Nowak’s death sparked widespread protests, allegations of “two-tier policing” and a spike in racist attacks against the UK’s Sikh community. Digwa, a Sikh, was carrying two knives, including a kirpan, on the night of the killing. Carrying the blade is permitted in the UK for religious purposes.Digwa, 23, has subsequently been accused by young local Sikhs of using threatening behaviour in a Southampton gurdwara, or temple, in the months leading up to the fatal attack on Nowak.The Sun reported that Digwa was seen brandishing an airgun in his back garden in October 2022. A neighbour who recorded him firing shots said she reported this to the police, but Hampshire constabulary was unable to find a record of the incident.Speaking in the Commons, Mahmood said the review would be led by the former Conservative lord chancellor Alex Chalk KC and would report its initial findings within five months.“Last December, Henry Nowak’s life was cut short in a horrific and senseless act of violence. My thoughts today are with Henry’s family and his friends, who have shown extraordinary courage and dignity,” she said.“It [the review] will investigate what was known about the perpetrator, including any missed opportunities to intervene.“It will look at the Nowak family’s experience of the criminal justice system and whether they were supported in the manner they should have been.“Once theIndependent Office for Police Conduct[IOPC] has concluded its investigation into the police response, this review will also consider the actions of the IOPC and, if necessary, the police.”Two officers, who were the first to arrive on the scene, are being investigated by the IOPC for potential gross misconduct.The investigation is looking at why they did not recognise that Nowak needed urgent medical attention and at the decision to arrest him rather than provide first aid.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFirst EditionOur morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it mattersEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionNowak’s family welcomed the review as a “significant moment” in their fight for justice.“Since Henry was murdered, we’ve fought tirelessly for answers to questions no family should ever have to ask. The emotional toll of that fight, on top of the unimaginable grief of losing Henry, has been immense,” the family said.“We hope this review, alongside the ongoing investigations and inquest, will finally uncover the full truth and deliver the accountability and meaningful change we have fought so hard for.“Our experience of the criminal justice system has been deeply disappointing, and we are determined that no other family should have to endure what we have.”Digwa was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years. He has been given permission to challenge the length of that sentence at the court of appeal on 5 November.Kiran Kaur, Digwa’s mother, was also jailed for three years for assisting an offender after she removed the knife used by her son. The knife was found by police at their family home along with more than 20 other weapons.Explore more on these topicsShabana MahmoodKnife crimeCrimePoliceUK criminal justiceIndependent Office for Police ConductSouthamptonnewsShareReuse this content

title: Typhoon Champi declared strongest storm of year so far | Extreme weather | The Guardian
description: One dead and 527 injured as winds of up to 185mph hit Taiwan and southern Japan, while Greece issues flood alerts
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: One dead and 527 injured as winds of up to 185mph hit Taiwan and southern Japan, while Greece issues flood alerts
Content: A pedestrian in Keelung. At one point more than 288,000 homes had no electricity.Photograph: Ann Wang/ReutersView image in fullscreenA pedestrian in Keelung. At one point more than 288,000 homes had no electricity.Photograph: Ann Wang/ReutersWeather trackerExtreme weatherTyphoon Champi declared strongest storm of year so farOne dead and 527 injured as winds of up to 185mph hit Taiwan and southern Japan, while Greece issues flood alertsMegan Davies and James Parrish for MetDeskMon 26 Oct 2026 05.28 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 09.40 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTyphoon Champi was declared the strongest storm of the year so far after recording sustained winds of 185mph last week. From late Thursday to early Saturday, the typhoon batteredTaiwanand Japan’s southern islands. Champi approached the east coast of Taiwan before the centre of the storm turned south along the Yilan County coastline, looping offshore and then tracking northwards away from the island. The storm brought gusts of up to 141mph and 48-hour rainfall totals of more than 620mm to parts of Yilan.So far, the death toll remains at one, with 527 reported injured. There were widespread power outages, with more than 288,000 houses having no electricity at one point, although most had since been reconnected. Champi has been downgraded to a tropical storm as it rapidly weakens to the south-west of Japan’s mainland on Monday.For the fourth time in October, parts ofGreeceare at risk of flooding. In the early part of this week, low pressure will bring severe thunderstorms and longer spells of heavy rain to much of the country, and this will be followed by a deep area of low pressure passing across southern areas.The national meteorological agency issued warnings for Monday, with 30mm-60mm of rain forecast in a 12-hour period across central areas, and50mm-80mm in the north-east Aegean Islands. Forecast models indicate the potential for similar totals in a 12-hour period between Wednesday and Thursday, making further flooding possible.A low-pressure system developed into a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal this weekend. Cyclone Arnab is expected to move towards the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coast by Wednesday. TheIndiameteorological department has alerts in place for extreme heavy rain, thunderstorms and strong surface winds across the eastern side of the country.Models are forecasting gusts of up to 85mph, and six-hourly rainfall totals of up to 100mm, as the storm makes landfall, currently expected on Wednesday. From then, the system is set to drift to the north before gradually dying out over north-east India at the end of the week.Explore more on these topicsExtreme weatherWeather trackerTaiwanJapanGreeceIndianewsShareReuse this content

title: Sunlight at night: US startup’s demonstration of lighting Earth from space draws criticism | California | The Guardian
description: Company imitates reflection of sun from mirrors, prompting pushback from some scientists, environmentalists and California locals
Author: Oliver Milman
Headline: Company imitates reflection of sun from mirrors, prompting pushback from some scientists, environmentalists and California locals
Content: ‘A coalition of environmentalists and astronomers are far less excited about Reflect Orbital’s ambitions.’Photograph: Reflect OrbitalView image in fullscreen‘A coalition of environmentalists and astronomers are far less excited about Reflect Orbital’s ambitions.’Photograph: Reflect OrbitalCaliforniaSunlight at night: US startup’s demonstration of lighting Earth from space draws criticismCompany imitates reflection of sun from mirrors, prompting pushback from some scientists, environmentalists and California localsOliver MilmanMon 26 Oct 2026 08.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 14.39 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLocals in a rural area ofCaliforniawere recently startled to see dazzlingly bright light shining down from nearby mountains at night, illuminating a swathe of the desert below.Unbeknown to them, the strange nocturnal illumination was the latest step in a company’s plan to erect thousands of giant mirrors in space to reflect sunlight on to the Earth during night-time.The night-time light demonstration, near the town of Lone Pine in the Sierra Nevada region, was conducted by a US startup calledReflect Orbital, which has an almost sci-fi aim to launch 50,000 satellites into space in the next decade to illuminate parts of the world at night.In July, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC)approvedReflect Orbital’s proposal to launch an initial demonstration satellite next year, which will orbit the Earth and, via a 59ft-diameter mirror, reflect sunlight in 3-mile-wide beams in strengths from moonlight up to the brightness of the sun at noon.The demonstration in California, undertaken earlier this month, showcased what this would look like on the ground, to the bewilderment of locals, one of whomcalledthe lights “blinding”. Large mobile lights were erected near Mount Whitney, with Reflect Orbital comparing the radiance to that of a full moon.This provided, the company said, a realistic simulation of one of the benefits of this technology: to help search-and-rescue teams and other emergency responders at night. Other planned uses include bathing crops in sunlight, replacing broken streetlights and even providing solar power for military operations, all summoned by the tap of a button on an app.“Search-and-rescue teams are expected to be our first customers, so this was a real-world test conducted alongside teams who would use our technology,” said a spokesperson for Reflect Orbital, which partnered with a local search-and-rescue team for the demonstration.“We’ll keep working closely with local communities and authorities wherever we operate, and are excited to show how this technology can help save lives.”View image in fullscreen‘The demonstration in California, undertaken earlier this month, showcased what this would look like on the ground.’Photograph: Reflect OrbitalA coalition of environmentalists and astronomers arefar less excited about Reflect Orbital’s ambitions, however. These groups have criticized the company and the FCC for threatening a harmful change to the separation of night and day that will affect everything from people’s sleep to wildlife and the ability to see the stars from Earth.“This is an idiotic project,” said Jan Hasselman, a senior attorney with Earthjustice, an environmental group. “There are a huge number of unresolved questions and significant potential impacts.
