The changes were impossible to ignore. Valverde and Aurélien Tchouaméni no longer the partnership in the middle, Valverde going to right-back instead. Güler playing. Diomandé playing. And, yes, Vinícius Júniornotplaying. “I’m not stubborn; I can change,” Mourinho said. Madrid have won five in succession now; something was seen that night, a way ahead. They’ve won every game since Vinícius was suspended, facile and perhaps even cruel though that may be to say. And since Mourinho grew a beard, if you believe in that kind of thing.View image in fullscreenKylian Mbappé celebrates the goal that leaves Real Madrid only three points behind Barcelona in the league.Photograph: Albert Gea/ReutersBefore theclásico, Mourinho had said it wasn’t fair to compare his team, a side in construction and a long way from the finished product, to Barcelona. He insisted that he was still getting to know his players; he hadn’t been there long, after all. After theclásico, he admitted: “We have improved, we can’t hide that.” The idea has shifted, almost like it was an epiphany: “I’ve learned something about the middle of the pitch; I have learned that a mixture is better, that it is better to have a combination of qualities than two players of similar characteristics.” In short, Tchouaméni and Valverde doesn’t work. There needs to be some football in there somewhere, and so a shift started. Sunday came as a kind of confirmation, a hope, an identity emerging.“The best Madrid is born at the Camp Nou,” ran the headline in El País. “Madrid are here now,” AS’s cover said. “I won’t let them have their heads on the moon; if we win this and then don’t win at the Sardinero, it won’t mean much,” Mourinho said, but this was a start, not just an end in itself. At full time, Mourinho headed on to the pitch and shook Lunin’s hand as all around players embraced. High in the north-east corner, Madrid’s fans stayed and sang. Back home, Courtois was watching. He had “a horrible night” on Saturday, they said, but now he was feeling a little better. They all were.PosTeamPGDPts1Barcelona1029272Atletico Madrid1012253Real Madrid1015244Real Betis102205Real Sociedad101196Sevilla9-2147Alaves103128Athletic Bilbao93129Celta Vigo1031210Villarreal1011211Deportivo A Coruna1001112Osasuna9-81113Racing Santander10-111114Levante10-31015Elche10-31016Rayo Vallecano9-8917Getafe10-10918Espanyol10-2819Valencia10-10620Malaga10-125Explore more on these topicsLa LigaReal MadridBarcelonaJosé MourinhoEuropean club footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Bournemouth school United in transfer nous, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Bournemouth school United in transfer nous, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa
Content: Liam Delap, James Tavernier and Evanilson, Zion SuzukiComposite: Getty Images, ReutersView image in fullscreenLiam Delap, James Tavernier and Evanilson, Zion SuzukiComposite: Getty Images, ReutersTen talking points from the weekend footballPremier LeaguePremier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s actionBournemouth’s transfer nous puts United to shame, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at VillaGuardian sportMon 26 Oct 2026 04.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 12.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1Cherries buy smart while United burn billionsThe three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so thanManchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them.Will UnwinMatch report:Manchester United 0-3 BournemouthWill Unwin:Carrick left carrying can for institutional failingsView image in fullscreenOmar Berrada and Jason Wilcox look on dejectedly at Old Trafford after another loss.Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images2Suzuki slots in seamlesslyAston Villa were quite happy to sell Emiliano Martínez but many feared it would be difficult to find an upgrade on the World Cup-winning goalkeeper. They have seemingly done so in the form of the £30m signing Zion Suzuki, who was superb againstManchester City. Nicolas Jackson’s goals stole the headlines but Suzuki’s bounty of saves ensured that Villa were victorious, while also impressing with his distribution. ”He’s ambitious. I think it’s very important, his mentality,” Unai Emery said. “Of course, we need a keeper first to save us in the goal, but as well we need one keeper to try to help us in our buildup. And in buildup, he’s a really fantastic player because he can play short, he can understand where is the superiority to break the opponent’s press. He has qualities to do long ball, getting our players in attack. So, we are very, very impressed how he adapted so quick with us.”WUMatch report:Aston Villa 2-1 Manchester City3Anfield warms to Araújo’s fighting spiritAside from the reaction to the half-time and full-time scores from Old Trafford, the biggest noise at Anfield was generated by Ronald Araújo showing no mercy in his challenges on Malick Yalcouyé and Charalampos Kostoulas. The on-loan Barcelona defender immediately endeared himself to the Kop with his commitment and quality, and was again in commanding form to help Andoni Iraola record his firstPremier Leaguehome win as Liverpool head coach. “I think we all enjoyed watching Ronald fighting,” said Iraola. “He’s very good in the duels. Even the first goal, he wins two duels in a row and defensively he’s been really, really good. I’m happy for him because I’ve taken him out in the last two games because we needed more offensive things. But he has continued working with no issues and today we needed him more. He has given a very, very good 90 minutes.”Andy HunterMatch report:Liverpool 2-0 Brighton4Striker problems at the BridgeJoão Pedro is unlikely to make a swift return after picking up an injury in training. The Chelsea striker missed the defeat to Tottenham and had a scan on Sunday. Xabi Alonso did not sound optimistic after the Spurs game. The expectation is João Pedro will miss this week’s games againstLiverpooland Manchester United as a minimum, leaving Alonso with problems in attack. It was strange he did not start Danny Welbeck against Spurs. Chelsea had no focal point and there are questions over their depth. Emmanuel Emegha, another struggling with injury, is yet to play since joining from Strasbourg. It is fair to wonder if selling Nicolas Jackson to Villa was the right move. Chelsea have played two league games without João Pedro this season and have lost both without scoring a goal. Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers are not as effective without him.Jacob SteinbergMatch report:Chelsea 0-2 TottenhamBarney Ronay:Glitch in Chelsea’s coding costs Alonso while resurgent Spurs are all systems goView image in fullscreenMateus Fernandes challenges Cole Palmer during Tottenham’s 2-0 win.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian5Arteta says he is not worst strayerMikel Arteta says he has been compiling a dossier of evidence of other managers straying outside the technical area after the Arsenal manager was shown a yellow card during the 2-0 win overEverton. It was his second of the season and leaves the Spaniard at risk of suspension if he gets one more, although Arteta suggested he is by no means the worst offender. “There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said, naming no names. “I am clipping all of that so I now have a massive storage of images, so if somebody comes to me I can say: ‘I am not in the record yet.’ Somebody else has the record so let’s see. Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers. I don’t know what we are going to do – let’s see.”Ed AaronsMatch report:Arsenal 2-0 Everton6González increases his value at NewcastleNico González cost Manchester City £50m when they signed him early in 2025, as part of that January spree as Pep Guardiola tried to arrest the first real slump of his Premier League career. Although he started nine league games that season and 17 last, González made very little impact at the Etihad. He probably wasn’t even the best Nico González in world football, given the Argentinian winger’s performances for Juventus and Atlético. But the Spanish Nico González clearly is a player of substance, his calm in midfield one of the few undoubted positives for Newcastle so far this season. Only Lewis Hall has made more tackles per game than him, he set up Sven Botman’s goalat Coventry, while he’s made more key passes per game than anybody other than Harvey Barnes. At £48m, he may end up representing extremely good value.Jonathan Wilsonskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMatch report:Crystal Palace 0-2 Newcastle7Sunderland earn a good pointTo ask a question that might be a segment on the Football Cliches podcast, is there a more “swirling litter” venue in the Premier League than the Stadium of Light? At this point it should be obvious this was not a classic. In part that is down the conditions – long balls ran away from players on both sides with frequency, and crisp packets were the only thing to trouble the nets at either end. Managing the Europa League was always going to be a challenge for Sunderland and returning from amidweek trip to Polandto earn a point against a team who have had a week to prepare is a good result, even if the Black Cats finish the weekend at the foot of the table.Tom BassamMatch report:Sunderland 0-0 Leeds8Bobb eases the pressure on ArbeloaIn spectacular style, Oscar Bobb’s wait for a first Premier League goal forFulhamcame to an end at Coventry. Bobb was signed in January, fitting the recruitment template that brought success and stability under Marco Silva, a manager adept at regenerating talent. Social media footage from the away end showed Fulham fans ask what Bobb, weaving and bobbing, was doing only for him to feint past two Coventry defenders and score. That broke the deadlock when Coventry appeared fully capable of claiming a point or better. It remains to be seen whether Álvaro Arbeloa possesses the some restorative powers as Silva. After two wins in succession, two clean sheets and a first win away from Craven Cottage since February, early-season panic has dissipated. For now. If survival is Fulham’s first objective, then successive wins over the promoted teams Hull and Coventry were minimum requirements. Though should Fulham aim much higher? Silva departed because his ambitions were not met.John BrewinMatch report:Coventry 0-1 FulhamView image in fullscreenOscar Bobb blows a kiss to the Fulham fans after scoring against Coventry.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters9Brentford struggle to make chances countBrentford are still yet to win away from home in the league but are also unbeaten on their travels. The draws at Leeds,Bournemouthand Aston Villa can be considered decent results, but this goes in the missed opportunity pile. So far Hull have presented a stiffer challenge at MKM Stadium than predicted, but in terms of expectations for Brentford this fixture has more in common with playing Sunderland at home than it does with their previous draws on the road. Against Sunderland and at Hull, Keith Andrews’ side struggled when the onus was on the them to make the game. The Bees play like they would rather not have the ball. In this one, they had plenty of shots – 14 in total – but only Dango Ouattara and belatedly Jaidon Anthony truly troubled Konstantinos Tzolakis. Brentford need Igor Thiago firing again.TBMatch report:Hull 1-1 Brentford10Delap under pressure to find the netWithNottingham Forestthe Premier League’s joint-lowest scorers, the pressure on Liam Delap is increasing. At Ipswich, where he was a rare bright spot with 12 goals in the relegation season of 2024-25, Delap was booed on every touch. The jeers got louder when each of his four attempts on goal missed their target. Only three of 18 Premier League shots in a Forest shirt have been on target. The raw materials that Chelsea moved for in summer 2025 remain present, the physical prowess and ability to find promising positions. The finishing touches are, at present, lacking, when Forest need someone to start scoring. Failing to take their chances at Portman Road left Forest in the relegation zone, endangering Oliver Glasner, when the ownership is trigger-happy with managers. Chris Wood, previously Forest’s talisman, came on in the 89th minute for Delap, but has been no super-sub so far, without a goal or assist from seven cameo league appearances.JBMatch report:Ipswich 1-1 Nottingham ForestExplore more on these topicsPremier LeagueTen talking points from the weekend footballArsenalManchester CityManchester UnitedLiverpoolChelseaTottenham HotspurfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Wolff hails Antonelli’s US Grand Prix demolition as the Italian’s ‘best race yet’  | Formula One 2026 | The Guardian
description: The Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has paid tribute to his driver Kimi Antonelli and hailed his victory at the US Grand Prix as the Italian’s ‘best race yet’
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: The Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has paid tribute to his driver Kimi Antonelli and hailed his victory at the US Grand Prix as the Italian’s ‘best race yet’
Content: Kimi Antonelli and his Mercedes team show their delight after his US Grand Prix victory put him within sight of the F1 title.Photograph: Eric Gay/APView image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli and his Mercedes team show their delight after his US Grand Prix victory put him within sight of the F1 title.Photograph: Eric Gay/APFormula One 2026Wolff hails Antonelli’s US Grand Prix demolition as the Italian’s ‘best race yet’Driver on verge of claiming championship in Mexico‘The drive was exceptional. He outperformed the car’Giles Richardsin AustinMon 26 Oct 2026 05.32 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 15.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Mercedes team principal, Toto Wolff, has paid tribute to Kimi Antonelli, who all but closed out his first Formula One world cham­pionship with avictory at the US Grand Prixthat Wolff described as the Italian’s best race.Wolff was at pains to point out the considerable efforts made by a number of other people in bringing the young Italian to the verge of a record-breaking title.After his victory at the Circuit of the Americas, Antonelli needs to ­finish ninth or better at the Mexican Grand Prix this weekend. He could even finish outside the points as long as neither his teammate, George Russell, nor ­Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, the other drivers in the running, win the race. If he seals the title in Mexico City he will become F1’s youngest world champion at 20 years old.Kimi Antonelli looks forward to drivers’ title after victory in US Grand PrixRead moreAntonelli led from pole position on Sunday with a controlled, ­dominant run largely at the front of the field, for his ninth success of the season.“On Kimi’s side, the main headline is that [it is] for me the best race that he’s delivered,” Wolff said. “Getting off the start with the ­inferior tyre and then controlling it at all times. ­Exceptional. I think he’s ­outperformed the car.”When asked if it matched­Antonelli’s superb drive from 19th to victoryat the Italian Grand Prixin September, Wolff acknowledged it was special, but that Austin was up there with that drive.Antonelli concurred. “Monza was a super special one and one I will remember for ever,” he said. “But this one, probably in terms of execution, was better because the way we built the performance throughout the weekend was very good.”Wolff believed it was all the more impressive given how difficult Antonelli’s rookie season had been in 2025 when at times he struggled with the car and made mistakes that caused some to question whether Mercedes had been correct to promote him to the team so soon.View image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli celebrates winning the US Grand Prix.Photograph: Bryn Lennon/Formula 1/Getty ImagesThose are doubts he feels Antonelli has comprehensively silenced. “There are many ­people that said last year after nine races ­without points he shouldn’t be in a ­Mercedes,” Wolff said. “People in other teams that said he shouldn’t even be inFormula One.“All of that now is extremely ­satisfying to see what he’s able to deliver, how he’s working with the team, with Bono [race engineer, Peter Bonnington] and yielding the results. But it wasn’t an easy road.“It’s been 30 or more years that I’ve tried to understand racing drivers’ brains and I still don’t know what has happened over the winter. His ­ability to process and deliver something that’s outstanding, which we didn’t see coming.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMercedes took on Antonelli as part of their driver development ­programme when he was 12 years old and have supported him through karting and in the feeder series to F1.Wolff was the driving force behind bringing Antonelli into the team to take Hamilton’s seat when the Briton left for Ferrari. Wolff was insistent he felt the youngster was ready to step up and he maintained that ­Antonelli’s success should not be viewed as ­having come from nowhere, but rather the product of many years and the input of many people.“I wasn’t the one responsible for it,” Wolff said. “It was teamwork. It was our junior team around [the ­Mercedes driver development adviser] Gwen [Lagrue] that dis­covered him when he was 11.“Credit to that group that have developed him over the many years. I read an interview [with the Ferrari vice-chair] Piero Ferrari last week where he said: ‘What a talent, he reminds me of Niki Lauda.’ And I’m thinking, people don’t get that this is the work of nine years.“The development of nine years, the hardship over nine years, the integration of the team, the ­working with the engineers, millions in the ­development of his career, of his ­ability, of his character together with his parents. It’s just not that it landed like this.”Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Kimi AntonelliToto WolffFormula OneMercedes GPMotor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Harry Kane claims men’s Ballon d’Or to end England’s 25-year wait for winner | Ballon d'Or | The Guardian
description: Harry Kane became first Englishman in 25 years to win men’s Ballon d’Or with Spain’s Alexia Putellas securing the women’s award for a third time
Author: Barney Ronay
Headline: Harry Kane became first Englishman in 25 years to win men’s Ballon d’Or with Spain’s Alexia Putellas securing the women’s award for a third time
Content: Spain’s Alexia Putellas and England’s Harry Kane with their Ballon d’Or trophies, which they won in London.Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPAView image in fullscreenSpain’s Alexia Putellas and England’s Harry Kane with their Ballon d’Or trophies, which they won in London.Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPABallon d'OrHarry Kane claims men’s Ballon d’Or to end England’s 25-year wait for winnerAlexia Putellas picks up women’s award for third timeEngland captain acclaimed in London ceremonyBarney Ronayat the London PalladiumMon 26 Oct 2026 19.11 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 19.54 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHarry Kane is the Ballon d’Or winner for 2026, the first Englishman to win football’s most prestigious individual trophy in 25 years.Two hours into a lavishly excitable ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London, Kane’s name emerged from the final envelope to wild cheers inside the auditorium. The women’s Ballon d’Or, awarded moments earlier, was won by Alexia Putellas of London City Lionesses, a third Ballon, five years on from her first in the colours of Barcelona.In the men’s voting, Kane finished ahead of co-favourites Lamine Yamal of Barcelona andKylian Mbappéof Real Madrid, an outcome that will perhaps cause the familiar consternation among the hierarchy of those clubs, not to mention the vast online fan army attached to the superstar players in Kane’s wake.But Kane is also a fully deserving winner of football’s ultimate gong. The L’Équipe-sponsored trophy is awarded by a vote of journalists and administrators across the footballing super-scape. For Kane, it is reward for a year during which he has won the European Golden Boot, played a major role in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga title, captained England to a World Cup semi-final, and above all shown himself to be a wonderfully humble superstar player.Quick GuideBallon d'Or: full list of winnersShowBallon d’Or MenHarry Kane(England and Bayern Munich)WomenAlexia Putellas(Spain and London City Lionesses)Kopa Trophy (under-21)MenLamine Yamal(Spain and Barcelona)WomenVicky López(Spain and Barcelona)Yashin Trophy (goalkeeper)MenUnai Simón(Spain and Athletic Bilbao)WomenCata Coll(Spain and Barcelona)Gerd Müller Trophy (striker)MenHarry KaneWomenCharlyn Corral(Mexico and Pachuca)Johan Cruyff Trophy (coach)MenLuis de la Fuente(Spain)WomenPere Romeu(Barcelona)Club of the Year MenParis Saint-GermainWomenBarcelonaSócrates Award (humanitarian)Bukayo Saka(England and Arsenal)Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“It was really tough this year, the incredible players I was up against,” Kane said as he received the trophy, going on to congratulate everyone else nominated for anything else, and thank pretty much everyone he has ever played with.“I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special,” he added.View image in fullscreenThe Wembley Stadium arch is lit up gold in honour of Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or win.Photograph: Harry Murphy/The FA/Getty ImagesAs a pure goalscorer, his numbers are astonishing this year, with 89 goals for club and country since the start of August 2025. At Bayern, Kane has also become a darling of the Bundesliga for his all-round game, creativity, intelligence and professionalism. Bayern paid a record €100m fee up front for Kane three years ago, a transfer that broke the club’s usual recruitment patterns and raised some concerns, given Kane was 30 at the time.It is a measure of his contribution on and off the pitch that this outlay is now seen as entirely vindicated. As a Ballon d’Or winner, Kane now enters rarefied company, heir to a prize that revolved around the Messi-Ronaldo two-hander for so many years, and which promises not just a form of sporting ultimacy but a vast uplift in current and future commercial earnings.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMore widely, the award is a coronational moment for Kane himself, 16 years into a professional career that has taken in loan spells at Leyton Orient and Millwall, running himself into the ground to make it in the Premier League, and now, for posterity, into the lineage of elite footballers.Earlier this month,Kane equalled England’s all-time caps record, while nudging his international goal tally on to 91 in 125 appearances. Aged 33, he still has a home Euros two years from now in his sights as England’s captain and a final opportunity for a different kind of footballing immortality.Explore more on these topicsBallon d'OrHarry KaneKylian MbappénewsShareReuse this content

title: Michael Carrick attends Manchester United training ground as club discuss his fate | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Michael Carrick was at Manchester United’s training ground on Monday to watch the club’s under-21s
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Michael Carrick was at Manchester United’s training ground on Monday to watch the club’s under-21s
Content: Michael Carrick on the touchline during Manchester United’s 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday.Photograph: Gary Oakley/EPAView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick on the touchline during Manchester United’s 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday.Photograph: Gary Oakley/EPAManchester UnitedMichael Carrick attends Manchester United training ground as club discuss his fateHead coach arrives to watch under-21s playBruno Fernandes likes Instagram post about loyaltyJamie JacksonMon 26 Oct 2026 12.57 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 16.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick was at Manchester United’s training ground on Monday afternoon as elsewhere at the ­Carrington base Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and Omar ­Berrada, the chief executive officer, deliberated over whether to sack the head coach.Carrick arrived at 1.50pm to watch the under-21s play a behind‑closed-doors game.Damning data: stats that show Michael Carrick’s luck was bound to run out | Andrew BeasleyRead moreWilcox and Berrada met at Carrington early on Monday morning after United’s3-0 defeat against ­Bournemouthon Sunday at Old Trafford that leftCarrick’s job in the balance. Wilcox departed just before 5pm and Carrick left shortly after.The defeat made it eight games without a win for Carrick’s side, who have two victories all season. United are in 16th in the Premier League, just a point above the relegation zone.If the 45-year-old Carrick is removed, Eddie Howe remains­Wilcox’s preferred candidate, with contact between the parties understood to have been made. The former Newcastle ­manager is open to taking up the position, ­subject to negotiations.Howe, 48, would be less expensive to recruit than Unai Emery, another admired manager, because Aston Villa would demand around £20m in compensation for the ­Spaniard.Julian Nagelsmann, the ­former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by ­Christopher ­Vivell, United’s director of ­recruitment, who is believed to have sounded out his fellow ­German. The pair previously worked together at RB Leipzig.Wilcox’s view may hold more sway with Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who ­controls football policy at United. Antonio Conte, who left Napoli in the summer, is another who may be in the frame.Carrick dropped Bruno Fernandes for the Bournemouth defeat for what he claimed were “pure football reasons”. This came after the 32‑year‑oldcriticised Carrick for his tacticsin the 4-1 capitulation at Como in the ­Champions League last Wednesday. The United captain was an unused substi­tute and was booed, along with other players, by fans in the ­Stretford End at the end of the defeat against Marco Rose’s side.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionOn Monday Fernandes liked an ­Instagram post that said: “Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care.” The post also said: “The person holding everything together is usually the one nobody thinks to check on.”Ineos, which is owned by ­Ratcliffe, has reportedly put FC ­Lausanne‑Sport up for sale. Ineos declined to comment when contacted by the ­Guardian. ­Lausanne-Sport are bottom of the top division in Switzerland.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarricknewsShareReuse this content

title: Damning data: stats that show Michael Carrick’s luck was bound to run out | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Favourable conditions and the rub of the green were behind Manchester United’s successful finish to last season
Author: Andrew Beasley
Headline: Favourable conditions and the rub of the green were behind Manchester United’s successful finish to last season
Content: Michael Carrick benefited from Manchester United’s light schedule last season.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick benefited from Manchester United’s light schedule last season.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAManchester UnitedAnalysisDamning data: stats that show Michael Carrick’s luck was bound to run outAndrew BeasleyFavourable conditions and the rub of the green were behind Manchester United’s successful finish to last seasonMon 26 Oct 2026 14.50 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 17.03 EDTShareManchester United have been the third‑best team in the Premier League with Michael Carrick as their head coach. It is some effort for his job to be so under threat when only Arsenal (57 points) and Manchester City (56) have been more productive than United (46) during the 45-year-old’s tenure.The tally obscures pertinent facts. United topping the Premier League during his 17‑match interim spell last season is irrelevant when they sit 16th with no win in eight games in all competitions this season. Losing narrowly against City is one thing, but three-goal defeats byComoandBournemouthwill surely spell managerial change.Michael Carrick attends Manchester United training ground as club discuss his fateRead moreCarrick can point to a degree of misfortune this season. Conceding stoppage-time equalisers toEvertonandTottenhamwas costly, although they also required an 89th-minute goal to avoid losingat Fulham, who were winless at the time.Opta’s expected points model suggests United have earned 3.8 points fewer than their underlying statistical performances merit in 2026-27. Only three clubs are further adrift of where they can reasonably expect to be.Equally, United’s expected position of 10th is hardly befitting a club whose net transfer spend this summer topped all those outside the Premier League bar Real Madrid, even before we consider their annual revenue and illustrious history. Their par level remains uninspiring.If they have been a touch unlucky with results, it was almost an inevitable outcome. United outperformed their expected points by 12.7 in Carrick’s share of 2025-26, 7.6 more than any other club. Such fortune was never going to last, as any back office paying the remotest attention to data would know. Poor recruitment in the summer increased the likelihood of a slump.Chart showing points minus expected points while Michael Carrick was in charge of Manchester United in 2025‑26The run of results appeared as unsustainable as it has proven. Eight of United’s 12 league wins under Carrick last season were by one goal. In that time, only Napoli (nine) had more such victories in Europe’s big five leagues. The expected goal margin was no more than 0.6 in United’s favour in five of those eight victories and they lost the xG by about 0.6 in their draws at West Ham and Sunderland. A lot of coin-flips went in their favour.United’s woes are not simply the result of luck turning against them. They are incapable of breaking down teams when dominating the ball. Something that seemed insurmountable for Ole Gunnar Solskjær has also hampered Carrick. Meet the new overpromoted club legend, same as the old overpromoted club legend.In Carrick’s first game, United won a Manchester derby despite having 32% possession. They were similarly ball-averse in victories against Liverpool (38%), Chelsea (40%) and Arsenal (43%) last season. Yet they have drawn blanks against Hull and Bournemouth in 2026-27 despite having 72% and 63% possession respectively. They were also unable to break down City when having a man advantage for three-quarters of the contest and 55% possession.United lead the division for shots, but no team have had a higher proportion of their efforts from outside the penalty area, which explains why their non‑penalty expected goals per shot average is the second‑worst in the Premier League.It is therefore fair to question Carrick’s tactical blueprint, asBruno Fernandes did after defeat by Como. “Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win,” was Carrick’s response to his captain’s comments. A look at United’s physical data justifies his concern.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIt is important to rememberthere is little correlation between distance covered and success. Arsenal lead the league for kilometres per match this season (119.4) but Fulham (119.0) are second. United are third-bottom, though their 112.3km per game average is up on the 102.2km they posted for Carrick in 2025-26.Far more notable is the shift in sprints. Data fromGradient Sportsshows United’s outfield players are averaging fewer sprints per 90 minutes than they did under Carrick last season. Youri Tielemans is not just below his figure for Aston Villa in 2025-26, he is barely at the level Casemiro offered despite being five years his junior.Chart showing sprints per 90 minutes in Premier League matches under Michael CarrickThe increase in average possession from 49.1% under Carrick last season to 56.7% may partially explain why United are sprinting less. However, City lead the Premier League for possession (64.7%) and average marginally fewer sprints than United, while Arsenal have the second-most ball (61.1%) and sprint more often. It seems unlikely United’s sprinting decline is entirely by design.Have the players stopped trying for Carrick? Or do they simply no longer have the advantage of free weeks thanks to the Champions League qualification his success brought? Wherever the truth lies, intensity has dropped. The favourable circumstances of last season have gone and Carrick does not look up to the task of navigating a far more challenging campaign.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarrickanalysisShareReuse this content

title: England Under-15s walk off pitch against Ireland in World Cup after racism allegation | Soccer | The Guardian
description: England’s match against the Republic of Ireland in new Under-15 World Cup has been abandoned after England alleged racism aimed at one of their players
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: England’s match against the Republic of Ireland in new Under-15 World Cup has been abandoned after England alleged racism aimed at one of their players
Content: England gather at the side of the pitch during their match against the Republic of Ireland, in the Under-15 World Cup, after one of their players alleged he was racially abused.Photograph: DaznView image in fullscreenEngland gather at the side of the pitch during their match against the Republic of Ireland, in the Under-15 World Cup, after one of their players alleged he was racially abused.Photograph: DaznSoccerEngland Under-15s walk off pitch against Ireland in World Cup after racism allegationMatch in new Fifa competition abandonedEngland players refuse to resume matchEd AaronsMon 26 Oct 2026 15.20 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 16.59 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEngland abandoned their Under-15 World Cup match against the Republic of Ireland on Monday after a player reported being subjected to a racist slur. Fifa confirmed it was investigating what happened in the final minute of the Group C fixture in Baku, Azerbaijan, when Ireland were leading 4-1.Footage showed an England player approaching the bench after an altercation. He is believed to have alleged an opponent called him a “monkey” and raised a complaint with the coaching staff, prompting England’s head coach, Matt Thorpe, to approach the referee.Thorpe was seen asking the referee to come over before instructing his players to leave the field. One of England’s assistant coaches subsequently told the referee: “We are reporting racism”, adding that the team did not want to continue playing.When another official approached to discuss the next steps, the assistant coach reiterated that England’s players did not want to resume the match. He also said a player was upset by the incident. Footage later showed heated exchanges between members of the coaching teams, with representatives from each side saying they were seeking to protect their players.“Fifa is aware of an incident at the Under-15 World Cup and Festival match between England and the Republic of Ireland,” said a spokesperson for world football’s governing body. “The match was abandoned by the referee following England’s refusal to continue.”The spokesperson said the official reports were being collected and that the matter would be referred to Fifa’s independent disciplinary committee, which would decide on any further action.The Football Association has not commented, but is understood to be waiting for more information. It is said to be taking the matter seriously and providing support to players and staff. The Football Association of Ireland has been contacted for comment.The inaugural Under-15 World Cup involves 189 countries and territories. Games are played in an eight-a-side format on smaller pitches, with two 20-minute halves.England, who had won their three previous matches against Cambodia, Montenegro and Nicaragua, faced Zimbabwe later on Monday, while Ireland were due to play Cambodia. Only the group winners will progress to the top-tier competition this week, with the rest of the teams divided into separate tiers depending on where they finished.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBefore the tournament, Fifa described it as “unrivalled in scale or ambition”. More than 3,000 players are taking part in 950 matches, with each team playing a minimum of nine games. Arsène Wenger, Fifa’s chief of global football development, described it as giving “players from across the world the chance to compete, to learn and to grow”.Explore more on these topicsFootballEnglandFifanewsShareReuse this content

title: Davide Ancelotti wants to make a name for himself – will he do it at Lille? | Ligue 1 | The Guardian
description: Lille’s results under Carlo’s son in Ligue 1 are encouraging but they have been exposed in the Champions League
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Lille’s results under Carlo’s son in Ligue 1 are encouraging but they have been exposed in the Champions League
Content: Davide Ancelotti took over from Bruno Génésio as the Lille manager in the summer.Photograph: Manon Cruz/ReutersView image in fullscreenDavide Ancelotti took over from Bruno Génésio as the Lille manager in the summer.Photograph: Manon Cruz/ReutersGuardian Sport NetworkLigue 1Davide Ancelotti wants to make a name for himself – will he do it at Lille?Lille’s results under Carlo’s son in Ligue 1 are encouraging but they have been exposed in the Champions LeagueByGet French Football NewsLuke EntwistleMon 26 Oct 2026 09.27 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 14.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIn a restaurant in Rio de Janeiro, two aspiring young managers sit around a table. Their respective clubs, Flamengo and Botafogo, are fierce rivals on the pitch. The relationship between the managers of the two clubs, Filipe Luís and Davide Ancelotti, however, is significantly more cordial.Speaking before his first meeting with Ancelotti inLigue 1on Sunday, the Monaco manager, Filipe Luís, described his counterpart at Lille as a “really formidable person”. The Brazilian added: “It is something special for us. It will be a pleasure to face my friend.”‘Leaving England is scary but I’m here to win’: Charlie Cresswell on Ligue 1 life and his international dreamRead moreThere were 12 managerial appointments in Ligue 1 over the summer; Filipe Luís and Ancelotti were two of the most interesting. Filipe Luís won the Premier League with Chelsea but is probably best known in Europe for his eight years at Atlético Madrid, where he won La Liga, the Copa del Rey and two Europa League titles across two spells. He carried on that success in his first job as a manager, winning the Copa Libertadores with Flamengo. “He knows what he’s talking about and how to motivate us,” says theMonacoforward Matthis Abline. “It motivates us even more to have a manager like him behind us.”Davide Ancelotti has had a different route into management. When your surname is Ancelotti, you can’t exactly make a name for yourself; his father, Carlo, has already seen to that. “I hope to be able to write my story, with my first name, too,” said Davide beforeLilleplayed in the Champions League earlier this season. No manager has won more titles (five) or managed as many games (218) in the competition as his father.Bar a brief 33-game stint as manager at Botafogo, Davide has spent the last 14 years following his father from club to club and then ultimately to the Brazil national team. From the banks of the river Mersey, to Bavaria, the fervour of the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, the grandeur of the Bernabéu and the vibrancy of the Maracanã. His trip around the world was enriching but he was always in the shadows. Until now.View image in fullscreenThe former Brazil defender Filipe Luís was appointed Monaco manager in the summer.Photograph: Manon Cruz/ReutersAncelotti’s appointment over the summer marked a radical departure at Lille. There was a common thread linking the club’s appointments of Christophe Galtier, Jocelyn Gourvennec, Paulo Fonseca and Bruno Génésio: they were all “a safe pair of hands” and most had considerable experience in Ligue 1. Génésio left Lille in the summer after his contract expired even though he had met the club’s key objective of qualifying for this season’s Champions League. The club’s president, Olivier Létang, simply said it “was the right moment” for a parting of the ways.Unlike the wider public, Létang was at least familiar with Davide Ancelotti thanks to their time together atParis Saint-Germainin 2012. Carlo Ancelotti was manager at the time, Létang was the director of football and Davide was the fitness coach. Létang did, nonetheless, use Carlo as a middleman when making his approach for Davide this summer. Carlo has even observed Lille’s start to the season from the stands, attending a draw with PSG in August.Quick GuideLigue 1 resultsShowMonaco 1-1 LilleAngers 0-0 LorientAuxerre 1-1 Le MansMarseille 4-3 Le HavreRennes 3-0 StrasbourgToulouse 0-0 TroyesBrest 1-2 NiceLens 2-1 ParisWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Lille have lost all three of their matches in the Champions League this season and sit second from bottom in the 36-team table but, after their 1-1 draw at Monaco on Sunday, they were just one point behind the Ligue 1 leaders, Rennes. The point earned at the Stade Louis II took Lille’s tally to 15 points from eight games; they have not started a domestic campaign this well since they won the title in 2020-21.Comparisons to his father are unfair but they are inevitable; the expectations on Davide have been moulded by two decades of his father’s unprecedented success. And it will always be extremely hard, borderline impossible, to live up to them. Every game is seen as proof of hereditary genius or – as had sometimes been the case in the opening weeks – its absence.View image in fullscreenEthan Mbappé gives Lille the lead at the Stade Louis II on Sunday.Photograph: Philippe Magoni/APThe game on Sunday did not offer much evidence of genius. Ethan Mbappé gave Lille the lead from the only clear chance of the first half. Thereafter, they retreated inside their shell. Even before Tanguy Nianzou was sent off for a reckless challenge on Paris Brunner, Monaco had them under the cosh. Ancelotti’s decision to take off a striker in the form of Soriba Diaoune for a defender in Isaac Cossier reflected the manager’s infectious fear.Lille could not hold on for the win and, in the end, they nearly lost the game. Monaco equalised through Edan Diop with 15 minutes to play and had numerous efforts during a late siege. One side dominated, but the points were shared. In the absence of any clear identity, Ancelotti praised his side’s “solidarity”. For signs of who Davide is beyond the son of the most prolific manager in Europe, the wait goes on. He is out of his father’s shadow but not yet truly in the light.Talking pointsThere was no “headline” fixture in France on Sunday night. The game between Paris Saint-Germain and Lyon was postponed until Monday. As was the case last year, it means that many of PSG’s nine Ballon d’Or nominees will miss the ceremony in London. Their absence last year was the result of a storm, which led to their game in Marseille being delayed by 24 hours.Unlike in the provincial cities, the planned protest in Paris on Saturday was not banned. With a significant police presence in the capital in an attempt to prevent a recurrence of last week’s riots and looting, and an NFL game to host on Sunday afternoon, the prefecture issued the directive, later adopted by the French league, on Friday.There was further disruption. Elsewhere in Ligue 1, Toulouse’s home game against Troyes was moved from Saturday to Sunday. In Ligue 2, Montpellier’s game against Red Star was moved from Saturday to Monday. There wasn’t the same degree of disruption in Saint-Étienne, who nonetheless delayed the kick-off of their game against Nantes by 45 minutes following a police directive.Another year, another call for bids for Ligue 1’s broadcasting rights, the value of which has plummeted in recent seasons. Dazn pulled out after just one season in 2024, giving rise to the Ligue 1+ experiment. The league-owned broadcaster, now in its second season, has been an editorial success but not a financial one. As a result, the president of the French league, Vincent Labrune, has announced a fresh auction for Ligue 1’s broadcasting rights, which will begin next month and end in December.The prospective deal would begin at the start of next season. Labrune spoke of a “new context” and one more conducive to bigger offers. Recent changes in legislation mean that the rights can be sold in a single “bundle”, offering the option of exclusivity to any prospective buyer. Without citing any broadcasters, Labrune also revealed “registered concrete interests from different actors”. Ligue 1 cannot afford another botched deal.PosTeamPGDPts1Rennes84162Lille85153Monaco84154Lyon78145PSG75146Paris FC84147Lens84138Marseille85129Lorient811210Nice8-21111Toulouse811012Auxerre8-61013Brest82914Angers8-6815Le Mans8-5716Strasbourg8-6717Troyes8-11518Le Havre8-72This is an article byGet French Football NewsExplore more on these topicsLigue 1Guardian Sport NetworkEuropean club footballLilleMonacoParis Saint-GermainfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: WSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progress | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start
Author: Sophie Downey
Headline: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start
Content: (Left to right): Eva Olid, Birmingham’s Wilma Leidhammar and Alessia Russo of Arsenal.Composite: Getty Images, ReutersView image in fullscreen(Left to right): Eva Olid, Birmingham’s Wilma Leidhammar and Alessia Russo of Arsenal.Composite: Getty Images, ReutersWomen's Super LeagueWSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progressGunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning startSuzanne Wrack,Tom Garry,Sophie Downey,Emillia Hawkinsand Mitul SamjiMon 26 Oct 2026 07.59 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 14.37 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWill derby win kick-start Arsenal’s season?The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result.Suzanne WrackMatch report: Tottenham 1-2 ArsenalGodfrey a star in the makingView image in fullscreenFreya Godfrey of London City LionessesPhotograph: Clare Overfield/SPP/ShutterstockIs Freya Godfrey England’s future? That’s what Alexia Putellas thinks of her London City Lionesses teammate, and the Spain icon heaped praise on the 21-year-old winger after she scored in her second consecutive WSL game. Godfrey – who made her senior England debut earlier this month against Greece – capitalised on a Khiara Keating mistake to score in the 2-2 draw with Liverpool on Sunday and her all-round display delighted Putellas, who told Sky Sports: “She can arrive where she really wants. I always tell her, she’s a star girl. She will be the future of this club. She has to keep working like she is doing now. She will be the future of England as well as the present.”TGUnited show progress under OlidManchester United’s display in Sunday’s derby draw was night and day compared to their most recent previous home league fixture against a title challenger, when they were torn apart ina 5-0 defeat at home against Chelseajust six weeks ago. Against Manchester City on Sunday they competed toe-to-toe with the defending champions, and while it would be wrong to suggest that Eva Olid’s team are anywhere near the finished article, their improvements are striking, both with and without the ball. Olid feels that heavy defeat early in her tenure actually helped her side. “It was a hard week after Chelsea but sometimes you need a difficult moment to happen, to react and see exactly where the problems [were] or the things we had to solve as a team,” she said. “It had to happen to now be the team we are.”Tom GarryMatch report: Manchester United 1-1 Manchester CityBirmingham earn first win of WSL returnBirmingham’s first win of the WSL season came in the first encounter between league newcomers this season. Followingan impressive point at the Emiratesthe week before,the 1-0 win over Charlton marked another key step as Amy Merricks’ side continue to settle into the top flight. The Blues were almost made to pay for their profligacy in front of goal against a familiar foe from last season in WSL2. They dominated proceedings and created 20 chances in total but registered just five on target. Océane Hurtré and Lisa Naalsund rattled the crossbar while Lily Crosthwaite missed three gilt-edged opportunities before Wilma Leidhammar struck a 68th minute-winner. “That was the most important thing today,” Merricks said. “We needed to pick up three points and we delivered that. I don’t think the performance was our finest. You could feel the caginess across the pitch and that is something we need to work on. We are in a better place, and we keep pushing.”Sophie Downeyskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDepth the difference as Chelsea produce comebackView image in fullscreenMelvine Malard displayed her class as Chelsea despatched Crystal Palace.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/ReutersFor 51 minutes on Sunday afternoon, it felt like it might just be one of those days for Chelsea. Despite dominating the first half – they created 12 opportunities to Crystal Palace’s four and registered 20 touches in the opposition box – they found themselves trailing and running out of ideas. A key difference between the two sides, however, is the strength in depth available to their respective managers. In bringing on Erin Cuthbert and Sandy Baltimore at half-time, Sonia Bompastor was able to call on the services of two experienced internationals. Cuthbert added a crucial bite to the midfield that had been lacking in the first half while Baltimore set up Melvine Malard to put the Blues in front before scoring from the spot to confirm the three points. In contrast, Jo Potter made just three substitutions with the first coming in the 77th minute. It is this ability to change things from the bench that truly illustrates the gap in class between the eight-time WSL champions and the league newcomers.SDSørensen makes statement against former clubBrian Sørensen and his Aston Villa side came away with a 3-2 win against Everton. Sørensen, who took over from Natalia Arroyo last month, faced the Merseyside club for the first time since hisGoodison Park exit in February. Villa dominated the clash and went 3-0 up within 50 minutes thanks to goals from Noelle Maritz and Amalie Vangsgaard, but they were given a scare following a late comeback push with Holly McNamara and Noémie Mouchon both scoring. Villa saw the game out to take three points – just. Nevertheless, Sørensen will be thrilled with the outcome, especially as it moved his team up to eighth. It also marked the first time since the 2024-25 campaign that Villa have won back-to-back games. “I’m happy, it was overall a good performance,” the interim head coach said. “Of course, maybe they got a bit too excited at the end but I also think we had the opportunities to kill the game off a lot sooner. But three points is three points, that’s all that matters.”Emillia HawkinsSymonds’ stunner inspires Brighton winMaisie Symonds’ stunning strike set Brighton on course for a 3-0 victory over West Ham. The Brighton captain broke the deadlock in the 29th minute, meeting a headed clearance with a first-time strike from distance that swerved beyond West Ham goalkeeper Constance Picaud-Inconnu and kissed the post on its way in. It was her second goal of the season, rewarding Brighton’s early dominance. Fran Kirby doubled the lead in the 63rd minute before Kiko Seike struck three minutes later. Brighton’s head coach, Arturo Ruiz, called it his side’s “most complete” performance of the season, praising their confidence and tactical adaptability. Symonds said Brighton “got control” in the second half. It was the Seagulls’ first Women’s Super League clean sheet of the campaign.Mitul SamjiExplore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueWomen's footballArsenal WomenTottenham Hotspur WomenManchester United WomenManchester City WomenBirmingham City WomenfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: McTominay stars in Napoli draw that leaves Allegri ‘not lucid enough’ to talk | Serie A | The Guardian
description: Gli Azzurri show positive signs of improvement in seesaw 3-3 draw against a Roma side inspired by Messi-like Matías Soulé
Author: Nicky Bandini
Headline: Gli Azzurri show positive signs of improvement in seesaw 3-3 draw against a Roma side inspired by Messi-like Matías Soulé
Content: Scott McTominay has scored a third of the goals Roma have conceded in Serie A this season.Photograph: Ciro De Luca/ReutersView image in fullscreenScott McTominay has scored a third of the goals Roma have conceded in Serie A this season.Photograph: Ciro De Luca/ReutersSerie AMcTominay stars in Napoli draw that leaves Allegri ‘not lucid enough’ to talkGli Azzurrishow positive signs of improvement in seesaw 3-3 draw against a Roma side inspired by Messi-like Matías SouléNicky BandiniMon 26 Oct 2026 07.21 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 14.08 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleScott McTominay was leaving nothing to doubt. He appeared to have scored with a close-range header early in the second half of Napoli’s game at home to Roma, but Pierluigi Gollini clawed the ball out from inside the goal. McTominay got his noggin to the rebound, nudging it back across the line. Roma’s keeper pushed away again, so theNapolimidfielder got to his feet and smashed the loose ball into the back of the net.Just typical. You wait two months for your first goal of theSerie Aseason, then three show up at once. They only counted for one, of course, but McTominay looked happy enough with that as he ran to thank Matteo Politano for the assist.Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha levellerRead moreWhat a difference it makes to this Napoli team when their Scottish star is fit and firing. McTominay was out of action for all of September, recovering from an ablation procedure to correct an irregular heartbeat – known medically as an arrhythmia. The condition was characterised by the clubas mild and benign, and the medical interventiona complete success.Napoli had struggled in McTominay’s absence. They continued to struggle right after his return, too. His first two starts back in the side came in defeats to Villarreal and Serie A’s last-placed team, Venezia – leaving thePartenopeiwith five losses from their first nine games in all competitions. The latter result prompted speculation about whether Massimiliano Allegri’s job as managercould soon be at risk.A week later, McTominay is starting to change the narrative.His two goals in midweekhelped Napoli to their first Champions League win of the season, 4-3 against Bodø/Glimt. On Saturday,he broke his Serie A duckand did everything in his power to deliver another win over undefeated Roma.McTominay’s three-strikes-in-one had made it 2-0 in the 48th minute, building on Frank Anguissa’s glorious overhead opener. PerhapsMcTominay’s willingness to attempt the audacioushas been rubbing off on his Napoli teammates too, though the Cameroon international was a title-winner and essential figure before the Scot arrived in 2024.View image in fullscreenFrank Anguissa succeeds in the spectacular to give Napoli the lead in the first half.Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/LaPresse/APThey could have been further ahead on Saturday. Mathías Olivera had a point-blank effort hacked off the line when the score was 1-0 before half-time. Then again, Bryan Cristante hit the post forRomamoments later.McTominay’s goal appeared to put Napoli fully in control, until Matías Soulé swapped a one-two with Donyell Malen and picked out the bottom corner brilliantly from outside the box. That was the 69th minute, and Roma were level by the 74th, their centre-back Leonardo Balerdi crashing home from a corner.And so McTominay answered again, with a wicked finish of his own from almost 30 yards. He matched Soulé’s precision after Roma had failed to clear their lines from a Leonardo Spinazzola attempt, tucking his shot inside the near post.Against lesser opponents, that might have been the end of it. But Roma are not easily beaten under Gian Piero Gasperini. In the 89th minute, Wesley crossed and Balerdi arrived to head home another equaliser.It finished 3-3, a marvellously entertaining game, with so many stories to tell. On the Roma side, this felt like a big night for Soulé, the 23-year-old Argentina forward delivering one of the statement performances of his Serie A career to date in a stadium named after Diego Maradona.Signed from Frosinone in the summer of 2024, Soulé has shown glimpses of immense potential but struggled for consistency, leading to questions about whether he can truly become more than Paulo Dybala’s understudy. But this season, and in the last month especially – which began with a first senior appearance for Argentina, then two assists in aheart-breaking Champions League defeat to Real Madrid– he is stepping ever more confidently from his compatriot’s shadow.“He’s in his prime, he’s the driving force of this team,” said Gasperini at full-time. “[Donyell] Malen didn’t have a great game, and [Soulé] carried the team. His goal was something crazy; the foot and leg speed reminds you of something [Leo] Messi would do.”View image in fullscreenMatías Soulé’s goal reminded his manager of ‘something Messi would do’.Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/LaPresse/APAnd then there is Balerdi, also Argentinian, on loan from Marseille with an option to buy. Gasperini noted how one of Roma’s strategies in the transfer market had been to target players perceived as leaders for their previous clubs. He named Marten de Roon in this category, too, and it was the Dutchman, wearing the captain’s armband, who put in the cross that led to Balerdi’s first goal.Unsurprisingly, given how the match unfolded, Gasperini seemed content with the draw. Allegri rather less so. He was sent off after Roma’s third goal and though he claimed not to know why, he was later overheard outside the changing rooms insinuating that the opposition had received favourable treatment from the referee. La Gazzetta dello Sport reported him protesting that: “Last year they handed you [Roma] the Champions League and I paid for it at Milan.”Without relitigating a year’s worth of decisions, this was a bold line to take. Milan, who spent almost the entire campaign in the top four and much of it as the closest contender to Inter for thescudetto, contrived to miss out on the Champions League by a single point after collecting only seven from their final eight games.Allegri cut short an interview on Dazn, saying that he was “for the first time in 25 years, not lucid enough to expand on this game”. Another claim that might raise a few eyebrows, from a man who once got halfway to undressing in frustration at the officiating of a finalthat his own team won.Quick GuideSerie A resultsShowTorino 3-2 Monza, Cagliari 0-2 Bologna, Como 2-0 Sassuolo, Napoli 3-3 Roma, Lazio 2-1 Parma, Inter 2-1 Fiorentina, Atalanta 4-4 Frosinone, Genoa 1-0 Venezia, Lecce 0-2 Juventus, Udinese 0-2 MilanWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Perhaps his ire on this occasion would have been better directed at one of his own defenders. During the buildup to Roma’s final goal, Sam Beukema collapsed to the floor after tussling with Balerdi off the ball. A generous reading of the replays would be to say that he “made the most” of some contact, which appeared to be arm-on-arm, though the Napoli player went down clutching his rib cage.If Beukema had stayed on his feet and continued marking Balerdi, perhaps the equaliser could have been avoided. Instead, he got up too late to do anything about it and then fell back to the floor again after watching the goal go in.An undignified end to a brilliant game. As frustrated as Napoli might feel at throwing these points away, there were lots of positives here to hang on to. Only a week ago we were asking whether Kevin De Bruyne could be persuaded to occupy the deeper role Allegri sees for him and make space for McTominay further forward. In this game, and the win over Bodø/Glimt, there were positive signs.Putting three goals past this Roma team – who had only conceded that many in the previous seven games of this Serie A season combined – is no mean feat. Napoli with McTominay are more than capable of improving on their current 10th place in the table and at least competing for a top-four spot.The challenge is to stay lucid, as McTominay did on his triple goal, sticking at a task until it is completed. And perhaps a little longer to make sure.PosTeamPGDPts1Inter Milan813222Lazio811223Roma813184AC Milan89185Como87176Frosinone84147Juventus83148Torino82139Cagliari8-31310Napoli831111Atalanta8-11012Lecce8-5913Bologna8-2814Sassuolo8-4815Monza8-3716Genoa8-7717Udinese8-9418Fiorentina8-10419Parma8-10420Venezia8-113Explore more on these topicsSerie ANapoliRomaEuropean club footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Australia give Steve Smith chance to prove fitness ahead of South Africa series decider | Australia cricket team | The Guardian
description: Australia will give key batter Steve Smith as much time as possible to ⁠prove his fitness ahead of the third and final Test against South Africa at Newlands
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Australia will give key batter Steve Smith as much time as possible to ⁠prove his fitness ahead of the third and final Test against South Africa at Newlands
Content: Steve Smith is set to return to the scene of his darkest day after his role as captain in the sandpaper scandal if he can overcome a neck injury.Photograph: Gallo Images/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSteve Smith is set to return to the scene of his darkest day after his role as captain in the sandpaper scandal if he can overcome a neck injury.Photograph: Gallo Images/Getty ImagesAustralia cricket teamAustralia give Steve Smith chance to prove fitness ahead of South Africa series deciderBatter aiming for Newlands return after injuring neck in second TestMarnus Labuschagne set to keep place; Nic Maddinson droppedAgenciesMon 26 Oct 2026 17.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAustralia will give key batterSteve Smithas much time as possible to ⁠prove his fitness ahead of the third and final Test against South Africa at Newlands, captain Pat Cummins said.Smith ⁠injured his neck in ⁠South Africa’s ​innings and 31-run victory in the second Test in Gqeberha which levelled the series at 1-1 going into the decider in ⁠Cape Town starting on Tuesday.‘Even my best friend didn’t know’: Usman Khawaja reveals why he kept his rheumatoid arthritis a secretRead more“Hopefully, it all goes well and he’ll be there,” Cummins said. “But we just want to wait for ⁠that last piece of the puzzle [before naming a team].”Cummins said Cameron Green would bat “preferably ​in the middle order”, which will likely ‌mean Matt Renshaw opening ‌with Travis Head after Nic Maddinson was dropped from the squad.For Smith, it would ‌be a return to the scene of his darkest day after his role as captain in the “Sandpapergate” scandal that rocked Australian cricket in 2018.“He’s been awesome this tour,” Cummins said. “In the last couple of years, probably particularly the last 12 months, it feels like he’s in a really good place and he’s enjoying his cricket.“He’s getting ‌himself out [and about], whether it is playing golf or going for coffee club every morning. He’s been super invested in what’s going on and ​very helpful for me out in the middle.”Smith has averaged a little over 20 in four innings with the bat and took a blow to the head in the first Test, before injuring his neck in the second.“He looks in total control of how he’s ⁠going about his work. He’s one of the greatest batters we’ve ever ​had. You don’t play ​100 odd Tests without matches ​where you’re not 100% fit,” Cummins said.View image in fullscreenMarnus Labuschagne is hoping to get over a psychological issue around the 30s.Photograph: Themba Hadebe/APMarnus Labuschagne’s ability to soak up pressure against the new ball and help the batters around him appears likely to give him one more chance.Labuschagne’s selection has remained the key talking point ahead of the third Test against the Proteas, after his run of innings without a century extended to 47.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe Queenslander has scored between 30 and 49 in six of his past nine innings, while his career average over the past 37 Tests is half what it was in his first 30.Australia have made no secret of their frustration with that, with Pat Cummins last week admitting 30s “aren’t going to win too many matches”.By the same token, Australia do believe Labuschagne is getting through the hard period and batting well, before a psychological issue around the 30s.“The focus is on hundreds. I don’t think I’m in a position to defend the performance,” chief selector George Bailey said. “But in terms of the collective, there’s been times where that’s helped. And that’s the question we keep asking ourselves.“We’re seeing some good things, yes. Is there a block at the moment around 30s? Yes. He’s still contributing in terms of his ability to get through a number of balls. So it’s a decision around what does that look like if it gets through there.“And what does it look like for the collective around and how everyone else, is it helping others around him. Is it helping the team get a result?”Explore more on these topicsAustralia cricket teamSteve SmithSouth Africa cricket teamCricketAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: England fret over Fin Smith’s fitness for looming Australia match | England rugby union team | The Guardian
description: Steve Borthwick has been handed a dilemma at 10, with the Northampton fly-half unable to join the England training camp this week
Author: Robert Kitson
Headline: Steve Borthwick has been handed a dilemma at 10, with the Northampton fly-half unable to join the England training camp this week
Content: Fin Smith came off injured during the weekend Prem game between Northampton and Leicester.Photograph: Luke Hastings/Wired Photos/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenFin Smith came off injured during the weekend Prem game between Northampton and Leicester.Photograph: Luke Hastings/Wired Photos/ShutterstockEngland rugby union teamEngland fret over Fin Smith’s fitness for looming Australia matchBorthwick responds by calling up Charlie AtkinsonGuy Pepper and Benhard van Rensburg also doubtsRobert KitsonMon 26 Oct 2026 14.30 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 16.17 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEngland are fretting over the fitness of the fly-half Fin Smith in the lead-up to the Nations Championship home opener against Australia on 8 November. The Northampton player ­damaged a calf in the second halfagainst Leicester on Saturdayand will be unable to join the national squad who have a three-day training camp in Bagshot this week.Marcus Smith produces timely reminder of his class as Harlequins sink SaracensRead moreLosing Smith so close to the ­Wallabies game would be a significant blow given the 24-year-old started at 10 in all three of England’s Tests in July and was instrumental in Saints’ domestic title triumph last season.England’s management say they remain hopeful he will be back in time to face Australia but, with limited preparation time available, there will inevitably be some disruption to Steve ­Borthwick’s plans.Borthwick has responded by ­calling up ­Gloucester’s Charlie ­Atkinson as cover, with Marcus Smith and George Ford the other ­specialist 10s in the squad. Since deposing Ford afterEngland’s defeat against Ireland in the Six Nations, Fin Smith has staked a firm claim and is very much the man in possession of the 10 jersey. Marcus Smith’s last start at fly-half for England was against Ireland in ­Dublin in the opening round of the 2025 Six Nations.There will be an official update on Smith’s condition on Tuesday with injury doubts hanging over several other players. Bath’s Guy Pepper appeared to be in pain as he limped off against Gloucester on Friday, while Benhard Janse van ­Rensburg has not featured since sufferingsustaining a heavy concussion in Bristol’s second Prem game of the season.The inside centre Seb Atkinson is also unable to train this week but has not ruled out playing for Gloucester at Northampton on Saturday. It leaves Borthwick and the squad’s other specialist centres – Henry Slade, Joe Marchant, Max Ojomoh and Fraser Dingwall – waiting to see what will unfold before the formal squad announcement next Monday.Marchant, for one, is delighted to be back in the frame for the first time since the 2023 World Cup. He then moved to Paris to play for Stade Français, ­having previously been told his England career was over, but is now back and eligible again after joining Sale Sharks.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe 30-year-old Marchant, who married Alan Shearer’s daughter Hollie this year, said he would love to feature at the World Cup in Australia next year. “When I was a kid I wanted to play for England and that’s not changed,” he said.Explore more on these topicsEngland rugby union teamNations ChampionshipRugby unionnewsShareReuse this content

title: Liam Dawson reveals England are ‘gutted’ after ODI series setback against Pakistan | England cricket team | The Guardian
description: Liam Dawson has revealed that the England cricket squad are ‘gutted’ after two agonising defeats have left their chances of making the ODI tri-series final hanging by a thread
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Liam Dawson has revealed that the England cricket squad are ‘gutted’ after two agonising defeats have left their chances of making the ODI tri-series final hanging by a thread
Content: Liam Dawson has become an integral part of England white-ball squad.Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/ReutersView image in fullscreenLiam Dawson has become an integral part of England white-ball squad.Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/ReutersEngland cricket teamLiam Dawson reveals England are ‘gutted’ after ODI series setback against Pakistan‘We were desperate to win’Spinner believes defeats are useful learning experiencesGuardian sportand agenciesMon 26 Oct 2026 09.15 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 17.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLiam Dawson has revealed England’s disappointment after the two ­agonising defeatsto Sri Lankaand Pakistanthat have left making the ODI tri-series final in serious doubt. “That ­changing room is gutted, we’re desperate to win,” he said.TNT Sports close to securing live UK rights for England white-ball cricket tour of AustraliaRead moreTo reach the final, England need Pakistan to beat Sri Lanka on Tuesday and then they have to thrash Gary Kirsten’s men on Thursday, but Dawson is optimistic the losses can help them in the World Cup in 12 months’ time in southern Africa.“If you look at the last two games, we’ve been in positions where we should have won, so that is a ­massive positive as a group,” he said. “To lose those two games from a position we’re in is frustrating because we should have won those games.“If, in a year’s time, we do get to those situations again and bank on our previous experiences then we’ll look back at this tri-series as a huge positive.”The 36-year-old said he is not drawing any conclusions from ­usurping Adil Rashid. For more than a decade, the leg-spinner has been the No 1 spinner for England in white-ball formats and he needs 26 more dismissals to become their all-time leading one-day wicket-taker.After missing September’s home series win over Sri Lanka because of an injury, Rashid has been overlooked for the defeats to Sri Lanka and ­Pakistan.The explanation given is Dawson’s skiddy slow left-armers are more suited to the conditions in ­Rawalpindi and Lahore, with Rashid expensive in his only tournament outingagainst Pakistan last week.In Rashid’s absence, ­Dawson has impressed, but a ­bowling unit light on experience has been exposed as England let seemingly surefire wins slip away.The former England captain Nasser Hussain told Sky Sports last week that Rashid’s recent performances had “dropped off”, although Dawson believes the double World Cup winner remains a stellar operator.“I don’t think I can be compared to Adil, he’s a phenomenal bowler,” he said. “You don’t play 165 ODIs and become a bad bowler. I don’t think you can compare us at all because we’re so different in our roles in the team. He’s a fantastic bowler, he’s been exceptional for England and I think he still will be.”Without an express paceman or mystery spinner, England let ­Pakistan off the hook from 154 for nine chasing 242 in Lahore on Sunday as Shadab Khan and the No 11, Haris Rauf, sealed an extraordinary win for the hosts.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe pair’s 89-run stand set a record for the highest 10th-wicket partnership in a successful chase and came three days after England, despite Harry Brook smashing a double hundred, were unable to defend 429 against Sri LankaAfter being a fringe England player for much of his career, Dawson has established himself as a mainstay in the T20 side under Brook and is more involved in the ODI setup.“Up until a year or so ago, I said to numerous people I didn’t think I’d play for England again,” he said. “I’ve really enjoyed the time I’ve had so far.“ You’re desperate to do well, but each time I get to play for ­England is a really special thing. I didn’t think it would happen at the age I got to so to play the amount I have in the last year and contribute has been really ­pleasing and hopefully that can continue.”Dawson retired from first-class cricket in May after 19 years with Hampshire and having played four Test matches, but he will not be reversing that decision even if approached by the new England Test head coach, Stephen ­Fleming. “Those days are gone,” he said.Explore more on these topicsEngland cricket teamSri Lanka cricket teamPakistan cricket teamCricketnewsShareReuse this content

title: TNT Sports close to securing live UK rights for England white-ball cricket tour of Australia | England cricket team | The Guardian
description: TNT Sports is close to securing live UK rights for England’s white-ball tour of Australia next month in a deal that could see one of the matches broadcast free-to-air
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: TNT Sports is close to securing live UK rights for England’s white-ball tour of Australia next month in a deal that could see one of the matches broadcast free-to-air
Content: England’s Jos Buttler hits a six during the ICC Men’s T20 Cricket World Cup match between Australia and England in 2021.Photograph: Gareth Copley/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEngland’s Jos Buttler hits a six during the ICC Men’s T20 Cricket World Cup match between Australia and England in 2021.Photograph: Gareth Copley/Getty ImagesEngland cricket teamTNT Sports close to securing live UK rights for England white-ball cricket tour of AustraliaChannel 5 in advanced talks over highlights packageOpening game may be also be free-to-air in dealExclusive byMatt HughesMon 26 Oct 2026 08.10 EDTLast modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 17.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTNT Sports is close to securing live UK rights for England’s white-ball tour of Australia next month in a deal that
